_doc: The lore web: one situation per marquee place, regional arcs and continent threads. Generated by tools/marquee/loreweb_build.js from tools/marquee/loreweb_src/*.json; schema in docs/LORE-WEB.md. Facts and themes only, all text original.

arcs.title: The Debt of Names
arcs.secret: Ayleid captives' names were never freed; a Colovian winemaking family has kept a name-vault alive under their vines for generations, and someone in Skingrad is quietly buying the vintages.

entry.text: A scaffold post has been chalked with a tally of a thousand strokes, and beneath it, scratched deep: 'Do not say them aloud. Take the rubbing to the Alessian gate.' A grape leaf is pinned through the tally.

arcs.title: The Gate That Was Opened
arcs.secret: The Oblivion gate at Kvatch was not opened by a stranger: the Ashen Candle, a lay brotherhood of Gold Coast fishermen who prayed for the drowned, was tricked into leaving a door unlatched. The survivors still hide among the rebuilders.

entry.text: A dock lectern holds a salt-stained prayer-sheet to 'the ones the water kept', every line struck through but the last: 'Light the Candle when the tide is out. The door is only latched, not locked.'

arcs.title: The Dragon-Hunters' Vigil
arcs.secret: The Akaviri who built Sancre Tor did not come to conquer; they came to bury something. A Blades archivist has been quietly relocating the vigil-bells of the Jerall passes to keep a seal from being rung open.

entry.text: A bell without a clapper hangs from the priory orchard wall. Scratched on its rim: 'Seven bells keep the door shut. Four are missing. Ask the statue what it watches.'

arcs.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings
arcs.secret: A pre-Alessian reservoir runs under every great Cyrodiil city. The Imperial Treasury has been quietly draining it into private vaults, and the drowned Ayleid water-magic is going sour.

entry.text: The innkeeper's accounts hang on a hook: a column headed 'water' where the bridge-inn pays more every season, in a hand that signs only 'by order of the Ring'.

arcs.title: The Sleepers of the Ashlands
arcs.secret: Since the blight faded, the ash itself dreams. The north-coast sleepers who walk uphill by night are not corprus victims but the ash's chosen audience, and a dwindling dream-cult keeps them from reaching the crater.

entry.text: A fresh grave on the cliff stair is empty. Slippers lie beside it, ash on their soles, and a child's chalk map pins down a route up the mountain with one word: 'Sleeping'.

arcs.title: The Seventh Canton
arcs.secret: Vivec's six cantons are a cover: a seventh sits below the lagoon, a quiet administrative afterlife where the Temple files every pilgrim who never came home. Imperial Ebonheart has been paying for it.

entry.text: A customs ledger on the pier has one column crossed out: 'Pilgrims Landed' and 'Pilgrims Left'. The difference is circled in red every month, and written beneath: 'Where do they sleep?'

arcs.title: The Guest of Brass
arcs.secret: A Hlaalu collector is reassembling a single Dwemer attendant from fisherman-salvaged fragments. The machine, when whole, asks only for one thing: to be told whether its makers are coming back.

entry.text: A fishing urn at the smoke-racks is full of tiny brass cogs, each stamped with the same little hand. A note says: 'Same buyer. Pays double for the ones with the thumb-print.'

arcs.title: The Council of the Quiet
arcs.secret: The Great Houses' ancestor ghosts have begun to vote: a shadow council in Old Mournhold's lower mirror-hall that steers the living by bequest. The Temple clerks of Necrom keep its minutes.

entry.text: A servant's lectern in the tower hall has a stack of bequests, all dated after the heirs' deaths, all signed by ancestors. Beneath: 'To the quiet vote, with respect. Seat unfilled.'

arcs.title: The Last Seed-Bank
arcs.secret: Before the first eruption an Imperial botanist sealed a seed-bank of unblighted crops in the cellar of an old Nordic temple. The yam farmers, the Telvanni gardener and the Redoran bulwark each know a third of the way in.

entry.text: An old seed-jar in the yam shed holds nothing but a label in a careful Imperial hand: 'Third of three. The other two lie with Raven Rock's ledger and the grove that grows in spirals.'

arcs.title: Six Stones, Five Songs
arcs.secret: One of the Skaal's six All-Maker stones has gone mute. The elder hid it. The lost hunter at the lodge went to wake it, and is held in the barrow's mural, still singing the missing verse.

entry.text: A hunter's cloak is spread across the lodge porch with a bone flute tucked in its folds. A scratch on the rail: 'Five answer. One does not. I have gone to ask it why.'

arcs.title: The Frozen Engine
arcs.secret: Karstaag's throne of ice is a Dwemer cold-engine. Haknir's crew sailed for it, split its charts among four hands, and lost the ship. The pieces are in the trader's crates, the lodge, the mead-hall's saga and the wreck.

entry.text: A stove-lid in the trader's shed is stamped with a ship's-wheel and the words 'Chart Four of Four'. A lever behind it opens a drawer of oiled bone charts.

arcs.title: The Uncounted King
arcs.secret: The royal tomb carves seven kings of the old line. There were eight. A stonemasons' guild paid by three Iliac crowns is quietly recarving the family tree to erase the eighth, whose heirs would void three thrones.

entry.text: The harbour-master's chain-log has a line where the same barge sails at night, three times a month, with a manifest that reads only 'stone dust, chisels, one priest'.

arcs.title: Cream-Coloured Invitations
arcs.secret: The Rivenspire fog is the carpet of a party that never ended. Invitations on cream paper appear in lanterns and doorframes, and those who say yes are collected by the fog. The Doomcrag necromancer sold the guest list.

entry.text: A cream-coloured card lies on the inn's single table, perfumed with plum. 'You are cordially invited. Dress as you were when you were happiest. Do not bring your lantern.'

arcs.title: Names Before Death
arcs.secret: A new name is carved on the memorial column every dusk, of Orcs not yet dead. A smith-spirit in the old city's collapsed forge keeps an account of those who will fall in the rebuilding, and cannot stop.

entry.text: A freshly chiselled name stands at the foot of the palisade, with a date nine days ahead. Below, in Orcish letters: 'Carved by no hand.' The stronghold's smith has covered it with a hide.

arcs.title: The Giant That Drinks
arcs.secret: The toppled giant beneath the inn is a Direnni construct kept alive by a Dwemer pump at Mthartzel; its tears are seawater from a drowned cavern. When the pump is stopped, the island of Balfiera rises.

entry.text: A fisherman's totem at the lighthouse base has been wired with a small brass drip-cup. Scratched on it: 'The tide is wrong. The giant is drinking again. Ask Evermor.'

arcs.title: The Thirst of the Buried City
arcs.secret: The buried city of the Na-Totambu draws the oases down its glass-roofed shaft, each season an inch. A herald of the dead dune-king collects the water-tithe from caravan masters and sells their debts on.

entry.text: A roadhouse tally-board: caravans listed with a tithe column. At the bottom, in a dead man's hand: 'Water owed: thirty-one wells. Paid: nine. Ask the goat.'

arcs.title: Reliefs That Remember Forward
arcs.secret: The battle-reliefs of the Valley of Scars carve themselves a little each season, showing a battle that has not happened. The arena-master in Dragonstar stages fights to fit the stone, and a serpent cult believes the last panel shows the world's end.

entry.text: A relief panel at the canyon mouth shows a scene half-carved: a dozen travellers on a staircase. The carving is fresh, and one of the faces looks very like yours.

arcs.title: The Gardener of Ahaleb
arcs.secret: A Hews Bane lord buys freed slaves' debts and sends them, not to work, but to tend a hidden garden of palms in a necropolis. It blooms only for descendants of the dead, and he is slowly planting his entire line in it.

entry.text: A rusted shackle lies on a sand-grave at the old slaver's cove. Scratched on the stone: 'Paid for, not freed. Ask who buys the debts.'

arcs.title: The Sunken Clause
arcs.secret: The treaty that freed Stros M'Kai carried a secret clause: every fifth year a ship must sail past the horizon with a cargo no one names. The inn's dragon tail is the prow of the first such ship, and the cargo is a torn page of the Tide-Ledger.

entry.text: A lever behind a harbour crate opens a small cabinet. Inside, a ship's manifest for a sailing in the fifth year: 'Cargo: sealed. Destination: not recorded. Return: not expected.'

arcs.title: The Late Moon
arcs.secret: Secunda rises a few minutes later each month. The Moon-Priests know and hide it, because the holy calendar sets the sugar harvest and the temple fees. The vault of lunar blades is waking to a moonrise that no longer comes on time.

entry.text: A little academy's observation log, kept by a mage who has never been believed: 'Secunda late again, seven minutes. The priests' almanac says on time. One of us is lying to the moon.'

arcs.title: The Faceless of Rimmen
arcs.secret: Burial masks of Rimmen's honoured dead are being stolen and sold abroad by the Baandari. A dead Khajiit without a mask wanders as a faceless guardian, and the moonstone-ring village at Hakoshae has run out of ways to bury them.

entry.text: A funerary mask lies in an urn behind the roadhouse's second lantern, the mask's mouth stuffed with a receipt: 'Delivered, Baandari stop, one of nine. The priests ask no questions.'

arcs.title: The Glow Beneath the Sugar
arcs.secret: Moon-sugar's glow comes from a coolant that leaked from a Dwemer colossus. The meadow blooms over the leak, the boil-houses of Senchal cut the refined with colossus dust, and the sleepwalkers of Corinthe are a symptom, not an addiction.

entry.text: A sugar-jar at the boil-house is warm and humming. A farmer has written on its lid: 'Does not taste like the meadow. Tastes of iron. Asked my wife. She slept three days.'

arcs.title: The Oath-Forge
arcs.secret: Every sword broken in Anequina's wars is carried by caravan to the hill. They re-form each year into a single blade of a hundred oaths, quenched in the bone trough of the dragon-scour. A faction of clan-chiefs wants to claim it; the blade wants none of them.

entry.text: A fort gate-post is scored with a hundred small crosses, one for each oath. A blade-shard is jammed in the crack and tied with a ribbon: 'Carry to the hill. Don't ask whose.'

arcs.title: The Crown Lamp
arcs.secret: The Elden Tree's glow is not the tree's own. An Ayleid star-lamp lodged in its crown by the first Bosmer settlers holds the Ayleid dead at bay, and its keepers have run out of names to feed it.

entry.text: A root-totem at the trunk's base has been drilled with a dozen small holes. In each a pale glass splinter glows faintly. A tag in Bosmer script: 'The crown is thirsty. Feed it names.'

arcs.title: Where the City Walks
arcs.secret: Falinesti is not walking by season: it is being led, by the chant of the apostates in a hollow tree-tomb, toward a hollow that will drown it in roots. Hermits and Orc outposts are secretly cutting guide-trees to break the chant, which the Green Pact forbids.

entry.text: An inn's travel-board lists the walking city's seasons, in one column the old route and in another, a new straight line drawn in charcoal, heading for a hollow tree.

arcs.title: The Citizens' Orchard
arcs.secret: The ring of living trees at Woodhearth are the Ayleid citizens of the burned city, turned by a Bosmer 'mercy' ritual rather than let die. Their roots remember, and they are leaning toward the ash-city, to go home.

entry.text: A thorn-wall plaque at the glade's rim lists forty names in a looping Ayleid script, each pricked out with a thorn. Below it, in Bosmer: 'The Mercy. Never be cut. Never be moved.'

arcs.title: The Truce of Bones
arcs.secret: Each generation the Bosmer and Khajiit elders of Reaper's March place a bone on the henge altar to renew the Truce. This time one bone is missing, and each stop on the trail holds a piece of the Truce's rite: a song, an arena's sand, a falls' name.

entry.text: A prayer-stone beside the falls is cut with eight notches for the Truce's bones. Seven are filled in white. The eighth is red clay, still wet, with a thumb-print.

arcs.title: The Skipped Hour
arcs.secret: Alinor's bells chime twenty-three hours, not twenty-four. The Psijic Order excised one hour from the capital's record to bury a single act. The hour survives as a room that rearranges itself in the relic vaults.

entry.text: On the meditation platform a sun-dial's gnomon has been filed to a stub, and beneath it a note in a careful hand: 'Count the bells at dusk. There are twenty-three. Which hour was taken?'

arcs.title: The Glass Fever
arcs.secret: Crystal splinters from a Daedric seed in Shattered Grove are rooting in the villagers. A Dagon cult in a red fortress coaxes the fever, and the victims hide under the cells of the prison under the spire.

entry.text: A bluff-top grave is covered in a fine scatter of crystal splinters, glinting in the grass. A small wooden marker reads only: 'Glass-fevered. Do not dig.'

arcs.title: The Egg-Tithe
arcs.secret: The cantilevered balconies of Cloudrest are held up by stone tuned to gryphon-song. Eggs are not hatching because the palace steward has been selling them to pay a debt, and the song is fading.

entry.text: An orchard-keep's accounts list 'egg-tithe, forwarded to the steward at Cloudrest': thirty clutches in each of five seasons, and none in the sixth. 'The gryphons stopped,' it adds. 'Or were stopped.'

arcs.title: The Silk Library
arcs.secret: Lillandril's books are vanishing because giant spiders are weaving their words into silk. A vanished librarian lives in the web, reading the silk aloud to keep it from being lost.

entry.text: A monastery urn is full of silk-thread spools, each wound around a tiny rolled slip with a word. A monk has tagged them: 'These are the library's lost books. Please do not eat them.'

arcs.title: The Tapped Root
arcs.secret: A merchant's stilt mansion has been tapping a Hist root for sap sold abroad. The falls that weep, the hag that spawns and the black pool are all the marsh's own ways of crying out.

entry.text: A sap-barrel behind the mansion's boat-shed is stamped with a golden sun and a tally of casks sold abroad. Beneath, in an Argonian hand: 'The Root is not ours to sell.'

arcs.title: The Warm Count
arcs.secret: The hatching pools are cooling and the eggs hatching pale. A banquet-ghost in the rotting pavilion draws heat for the plates of a supper that never ends.

entry.text: An egg-shaped stone on the hill has a warm-count carved in it, each season's temperature a notch lower than the last. A fresh notch is chiselled this week, deeper than any.

finale.boss: The Lord of the Long Supper

arcs.title: The Extra One
arcs.secret: Every census in the Shadowfen counts one more than the roll. The extra is the village's first settler, who was never named, and whose seat has been kept for generations at a rice-paddy table, a village fire and a Hist pool.

entry.text: A rice-counter's tally: forty-one workers at sunrise, forty-two at dusk. Below, in a careful hand: 'Did I miscount? I never miscount.'

arcs.title: The Rerouted Dirge
arcs.secret: The grave-singers carry the dead down the delta to the island necropolis by song. A Gideon plantation lord has quietly rerouted the dirge's path through his dry fields, in the belief that the dead's blessing will bring rain.

entry.text: A fishing-hamlet grave is empty, its marker moved a hundred paces inland from the shore. Scratched on the stone: 'The dirge doesn't go to the water any more.'

finale.boss: Lord Heel of the Dry Fields

arcs.title: The Last Voyage Home
arcs.secret: The last Atmoran hold stands on an ice shelf that is about to calve. A frozen dragon in the mound keeps the shelf bound; the whole ship of the dead captain in the howe is the only vessel left to carry the living out.

entry.text: A broken ship's ribs, and in the sand a dead sailor with a rune-tablet clutched in both hands: 'Ice cracks under the long halls. The captain's ship sleeps in the howe. Wake her before the thaw.'

arcs.title: The Four-Court Seal
arcs.secret: Each of Akavir's four courts holds one quarter of a seal-name that keeps the dragon-graveyard shut. The Tsaesci serpent-court wishes to gather all four and open the valley. The ice throne of Kamal holds the last quarter.

entry.text: A watch-tower's border stone carries a fourfold seal, three quarters worn smooth. On the fourth, a handful of Akaviri characters: 'Three bow. One waits in the ice.'

arcs.title: The Walking Reef
arcs.secret: A reef of plague-coral from the Thras sea is spreading across the Maormer isles, slowly walking toward the fleet raft. The serpent pens feed on it and grow monstrous, and the citadel's window on the deep shows the reef's head.

entry.text: A pen-keeper's totem is hung with pink coral-shards that have started to take root in the wood. A scratch on its post: 'The pens are eating it. The pens are growing. Who feeds the pens?'

arcs.title: The Last Lesson
arcs.secret: The Ra Gada sword-masters' final lesson is a voyage: each school teaches one form, and the last student rows the funeral barge of the Yokudan kings home. No student has finished in three hundred years.

entry.text: A training-post is carved with four forms. Three have a student's name. The fourth reads only: 'The Last Lesson, taught on the water.' A master's sandal sits on the step.

threads.title: The Welkynd Census
threads.secret: Ayleid lamp-wardens tuned their light-stones into one continental instrument. A scholars' cabal from the Summerset libraries, calling itself the Lampwrights, is relighting the dead stones in order. When the last is lit, the Crystal Tower's lens will show the sky as it was before the fall, and wake the name-vaults.

entry.text: A scholar's census slate leans against the gate-arch: eight stone-names in a column, five struck through in a fresh hand. The last line reads, in Aldmeri: 'Then the Tower.'

threads.title: The Ash Remembers
threads.secret: Ash from Red Mountain carries a faint memory of the people it burned. A Telvanni theory holds that the memory seeds where it falls, in groves, in marshes and in the dreams of exiles, and that a Hist-tree in the south is the only thing that can read it all.

entry.text: A glass urn at a ghostfence gate-post holds a pinch of grey ash and a card: 'Falls where it chooses. Remembers what it burned. Follow the fall.' A map of the prevailing winds is pinned beneath.

threads.title: The Dwemer Dial
threads.secret: Each Dwemer ruin keeps a bronze dial in its deepest hall, all set to the same figure and all turning forward since the Heart was silenced. At the end of its sweep, the spire at Rkuldumz will answer. The dials were a countdown to a return, or a recall.

entry.text: A lever behind a stilled conveyor drops a bronze plate. Its face is a dial with one hand, its figure scratched with a tiny cross and, in scholar's script: 'Eight of these. All the same figure. All ticking.'

threads.title: The Sugar Road
threads.secret: A hidden counting-house buys the debts of every sugar farm, caravan and dockside inn from the Elsweyr coast to the Bitter Coast. Its patron is a pale lender who collects years of labour rather than gold, and keeps his strongbox on the stilts of a swamp market.

entry.text: A sugar-urn at the meadow's edge holds a debt-slip folded around a coin. The slip bears a watermark: a crescent moon and a ledger. 'Purchased. Do not pay the farmer. Pay the Counting-House.'

threads.title: The Bone Census
threads.secret: Every ancient dragon grave on Tamriel and Akavir is missing one vertebra. The Tsaesci serpent-court has been collecting them to build a spine, a ladder to somewhere high, and its agents have visited every barrow and mound in the last ten years.

entry.text: A great dragon's rib-arch with a gap in its spine: one vertebra, neatly removed, a clean saw-cut. A tag in a courtly hand: 'Number 14 of 41. Inspected. Collected.'

threads.title: The Tide-Ledger
threads.secret: The last navigator of the Yokudan fleet tore his tide-ledger in nine and hid the pieces in nine ports across the seas, so no single people could chart the road home. The Maormer want the road; the Redguards want the route to a hidden isle of kings; the Altmer want to bury it again.

entry.text: A scale-mosaic tile at the temple's threshold bears an unfamiliar tide-glyph and a navigator's mark. Scratched into its edge: 'One of nine. Seek the other eight. Read at low tide only.'

threads.title: The Sundered Crown
threads.secret: A conqueror known by a dozen names, remembered by every people as a foreign king, was buried in eight pieces under eight realms' royal tombs so he could not rise. Someone is gathering the regalia, a finger-ring in a barrow, a crown in a ship, a throne-arm in the ice, to make him whole.

entry.text: A king's tomb has a seal cut cleanly in two, the other half missing. Beside it is a fresh chisel-mark and a note: 'Number three. The ring is gone. The ring of the Hollow King.'

threads.title: The Silent Falls
threads.secret: The continent's great waterfalls and cascades are falling silent one night at a time, each hush a verse of a binding lullaby. A coven of water-witches is singing the Weeping One, a buried wamasu fossil under the Black Marsh falls, into a sleep it will never wake from, and the world's tears with it.

entry.text: A pilgrim's notebook left on a flat rock: eight falls named, six crossed out with the date and a single word, 'hushed'. 'Tonight: the pool at Mist Mirror. Do not be near the water when it stops.'

shardiuss_excavation.name: Shardiuss Excavation
shardiuss_excavation.site: A cut-away of a Blackwood hillside held in scaffolds above a stepped Ayleid terrace, with ladders going down into pale-white stone.
shardiuss_excavation.mystery: The diggers were paid in wine and stopped the day someone read a carved name aloud. No one will say what the pit answered.
clues: scaffold posts tallied with a thousand chalk strokes
crates stamped with a grape-leaf seal
a wall where 'DO NOT SPEAK' is written in four hands
shardiuss_excavation.payoff: A rubbing of the first name-glyph set and a hidden dig-chamber holding an Ayleid lamp.
shardiuss_excavation.rumour: They say the diggers at Shardiuss all quit on one day, paid in barrels instead of coin, and none will go near the pit.
shardiuss_excavation.thread_clue: a lamp relit in the pit, its flame a cold new white

gate_of_alma_ruma.name: Gate of Alma Ruma
gate_of_alma_ruma.site: A worn Alessian gate of white stone with a scroll-temple annex leaning against its flank, still ringed by a dry processional road.
gate_of_alma_ruma.mystery: The annex keeps a register of Ayleid names taken in the wars, each to be struck through when freed. Almost none are struck.
clues: rows of name-plates pinned to the annex walls
a brazier of ash where unburnt scrolls are stacked
an arch whose last inscription line was chiselled away
gate_of_alma_ruma.payoff: A chiselled-away line that, read with the rubbing, names a vineyard.
gate_of_alma_ruma.rumour: The Alma Ruma annex has a ledger of names and the old priest there weeps when anyone asks to see the page that was cut out.
gate_of_alma_ruma.thread_clue: a census slate with five of eight stone-names struck through

thalaras_winery.name: Thalaras Winery
thalaras_winery.site: A single-family cellar estate with a stone press, where the vines have grown over a flagstone floor that is, in fact, a lamp-hall roof.
thalaras_winery.mystery: Every barrel is labelled with a dead person's name, and the 'Remembrance' vintage lets a drinker recall the one it is named for. The family keeps a name unsaid.
clues: cellar barrels tagged with names not dates
grapes with crystalline skins on the oldest vines
a cellar lintel carved in Ayleid script, half-hidden by ivy
thalaras_winery.payoff: The 'Remembrance' bottle, a one-use item that shows a stranger's last day.
thalaras_winery.rumour: The Thalaras cellar sells a wine that tastes like a memory. No one who drinks it will say whose.

mist_mirror_refuge.name: Mist Mirror Refuge
mist_mirror_refuge.site: A hidden waterfall pool in the Nibenay valley that mirrors a different night sky from the one overhead, ringed in cut stones under the water.
mist_mirror_refuge.mystery: In the reflection, certain stars carry names that burn briefly and go out. Pilgrims believe each is an Ayleid soul passing on.
clues: pilgrims' ribbons tied to a ring of sunken stones
a rowing-boat whose oars are carved in glyphs
a wading-line of footprints that goes into the pool and does not come out
mist_mirror_refuge.payoff: A ring of 'star-names' to read at night, enough to open a cellar door.
mist_mirror_refuge.rumour: The pool at Mist Mirror shows the wrong stars. I do not go at night, and I do not go alone.
mist_mirror_refuge.thread_clue: a pool whose waterfall stops at midnight and starts at dawn

skingrad.name: Skingrad
skingrad.site: A vineyard-ringed hill town whose castle crowns a rock, with long vine rows from the air that form one repeating glyph.
skingrad.mystery: The Count has never been seen. The castle's steward buys the entire Thalaras vintage and burns the empty bottles.
clues: vineyard rows planted in a glyph visible from the castle rock
wax seals smelling of wine rather than tallow
a bell in the keep that rings nightly with no ringer
skingrad.payoff: The steward's sealed key, opening the Count's wine vault.

miscarcand.name: Miscarcand
miscarcand.site: A buried Ayleid city-vault of lit welkynd stone, tiered cisterns and bridges over drowned galleries.
miscarcand.mystery: The Last Warden counts every name it holds and wants one to be restored: its own. Whoever frees or binds it decides what the dead are owed.
clues: lamp-gates that open only to a spoken syllable
plates of names stacked in the cold vault
a cistern whose water rises when a name is read
miscarcand.payoff: The sealed name-plate, a unique welkynd-lit relic that can free or bind shades.
miscarcand.rumour: Miscarcand's gate lamps burn blue when a name is read, and some say the dead there are waiting to be asked.
miscarcand.thread_clue: a lamp-gate relit with the cabal's cold white flame

lunar_fang_docks.name: Lunar Fang Docks
lunar_fang_docks.site: Rickety lake docks lit by a string of pale moonlamps, with a dozen boats that never leave and a single candle on the harbour-master's step.
lunar_fang_docks.mystery: Each low tide the fishermen light one candle for someone they will not name. They flinch at any talk of Kvatch.
clues: a single candle on the harbour step, lit at low tide only
boats named for the drowned, never launched
moonlamps painted over with soot on the Kvatch side
lunar_fang_docks.payoff: The Ashen Candle's token, a salt-crusted wick, which opens a hidden sanctuary door.
lunar_fang_docks.rumour: The Lunar Fang boats don't fish the south reach any more. They light a candle and sit in the dark instead.
lunar_fang_docks.thread_clue: moonlamps painted with a crescent, a ledger on the lamp-post

dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.name: Cyrodiil Sanctuary
dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.site: A hidden cellar sanctuary under a nondescript house on the Gold Coast, with a small crypt-warren, a communal hall and a locked inner coffin-room.
dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.mystery: The Family here took a contract on a man who was already dead: a Kvatch priest who said the gate would be latched, not locked. They kept his last letter.
clues: a locked coffin-room with a candle burning inside
contract slips filed under a Kvatch lintel-stone
a shrine whose offerings are all salted fish
dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.payoff: The Kvatch priest's letter, naming the Ashen Candle's surviving members.
dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.rumour: A house on the Gold Coast road has no windows and a smoke-hole that smells of fish. People cross the street.

anvil.name: Anvil
anvil.site: A crescent harbour town with a white mole curling out to a lighthouse, blue-roofed houses on two terraces and a castle at the seaward point.
anvil.mystery: Anvil's lighthouse is lit every night by a keeper nobody has hired. It was first lit the night Kvatch burned.
clues: a lighthouse lamp trimmed by no visible hand
children's chalk candles on the quays
a ship's figurehead pulled from the water that bears a burning wick
anvil.payoff: A lighthouse key that opens the lamp-room hatch.

deepscorn_hollow.name: Deepscorn Hollow
deepscorn_hollow.site: A coastal cave with a drowned lower level, a moon-lit sink-hole and a bone-white hall that shows different rooms at different tides.
deepscorn_hollow.mystery: A vampire court hid here from the Crisis and took in the survivors of the Candle. Their price: a steady supply of bells.
clues: tide-marks scored on the cave wall with names beneath
candle stubs in the sink-hole's mud
a hall where the table is laid for twelve and only ten have settings
deepscorn_hollow.payoff: A bone candle that stays lit under water and burns only for the Candle's survivors.
deepscorn_hollow.rumour: The Hollow's caves flood and empty twice a day. Folk say a candle burns down there that never goes out.

kvatch.name: Kvatch
kvatch.site: A slope city half-rebuilt in pale new timber against black scorched stone, with a crater at its heart and a castle clinging to its upper wall.
kvatch.mystery: A hidden register of the night the Gate opened lies under the new masonry. The town will not rebuild the north ward; the masons say the foundations hum.
clues: new timber scaffolds against scorched basalt
a ward where no mason will lay a stone
a chapel bell cast from the Gate's melted slag
kvatch.payoff: The register itself, a book that names who latched the door.

kvatch_gate.name: Kvatch Gate
kvatch_gate.site: The burning crater edge where the Gate first opened, with a wrecked siege-tower, a plume of ash and a ring of lava glass.
kvatch_gate.mystery: A ring of lava glass at the crater edge holds a last candle that never gutters. It marks the door that was only latched.
clues: lava glass fused into a ring of candle-stubs
a siege-tower leaning toward the crater with a latch carved on its spar
a plume of ash that falls upward at dusk
kvatch_gate.payoff: A shard of Gate-glass that, held up, shows the door as it was before the night.
kvatch_gate.rumour: At dusk the ash at the crater rises instead of falling. The masons say it is looking for someone.

weynon_priory.name: Weynon Priory
weynon_priory.site: A grey-stone cloister with a bell tower and an orchard on the Colovian slopes, where a single clapperless bell hangs from the orchard wall.
weynon_priory.mystery: Seven bells hold a seal shut in the Jerall passes. The priory's clapper was taken by an archivist of the Blades, who is quietly relocating all seven.
clues: a clapperless bell hanging in the orchard
monks' soles worn from walking a path to the high pass
a bell tower where a rope has been replaced by a chain
weynon_priory.payoff: The clapper, which rings only for the other six bells.
weynon_priory.rumour: The priory's bell rings once at night with no hand on it. The brothers say to leave it be.

the_sentinel.name: The Sentinel
the_sentinel.site: A lone statue guardian on a ridge above the Valus road, hand raised against something no traveller can see.
the_sentinel.mystery: The Sentinel's raised hand points to a notch in the far ridge where a bell once hung. Ravens avoid it, and wind drops around its feet.
clues: a raised hand aimed at a notch in the far ridge
ring-bolts in the plinth where a rope once ran
a ridge where ravens never settle
the_sentinel.payoff: A bell-pull bolt that fits the Bruma chapel's rope.
the_sentinel.rumour: Wind drops dead at the foot of the Sentinel, and the ravens won't land on it.

bruma.name: Bruma
bruma.site: A mountain town climbing a switchback valley under the Jerall ridge, with terraces stacked above a fast stream and a tall chapel spire.
bruma.mystery: The chapel's bell was recast in secret last winter. The old bell now lies in the foundation of the Talos shrine, and nobody will say who ordered it moved.
clues: a chapel bell that rings a slightly wrong note
fresh mortar in the shrine's foundation stones
a chain where a bell-rope hung
bruma.payoff: The old chapel bell's clapper, wrapped in sackcloth in a crypt.

cloud_ruler_temple.name: Cloud Ruler Temple
cloud_ruler_temple.site: The Blades' cliff keep above the cloud line, with banners, wind and a rope bridge over the whole Jerall range.
cloud_ruler_temple.mystery: A Blades archivist is hanging the bells in its highest cloister, away from any road. She calls it 'the long watch' and will not say who she keeps it against.
clues: a cloister where bells hang silent in a row
rope-bridge planks recently replaced
a Blades officer's journal entry crossed out in red
cloud_ruler_temple.payoff: A key to the archive's lowest ledger, listing the seven vigils.
cloud_ruler_temple.rumour: The Cloud Ruler cloister has a row of bells that don't ring, and a woman in grey who polishes them.

frostcrag_spire.name: Frostcrag Spire
frostcrag_spire.site: A single obsidian spire on a rock in a cold sea, with no stairs: only a levitation or boat to the door and a storm-room at the top.
frostcrag_spire.mystery: The wizard who bought the bell fell in love with its note. The spire hums in it. The bell is bolted to the storm-room floor and the wizard will not let it go.
clues: a hum that matches the Weynon clapper's pitch
a sea-door with a bell-shaped keyhole
a storm-room whose floor is a bell's inverted mouth
frostcrag_spire.payoff: The Frostcrag bell itself, a staff-length of Akaviri bronze.
frostcrag_spire.rumour: The Spire sings in storm weather. Fishermen say it hums the same note as the old priory bell.

sancre_tor.name: Sancre Tor
sancre_tor.site: A mountaintop Akaviri fortress above a barrow of dragon-hunters, with pagoda-curved halls over long tomb galleries.
sancre_tor.mystery: The Akaviri came to bury a thing, not to rule. The seventh bell hangs in the barrow's deepest nave, tied to a seal no one remembers.
clues: pagoda eaves with bell-shaped hooks and no bells
tomb galleries whose lamp-niches face one direction
a rope worn through at the same height on every beam
sancre_tor.payoff: A dragonguard sabre in the deepest nave and the vigil's closing words.
sancre_tor.rumour: Sancre Tor's walls once rang. The hunters swore the barrow's gate rings three notes on the night before a storm.
sancre_tor.thread_clue: a barrow's dragon-bone niche empty, its tag still in place

imperial_bridge_inn.name: Imperial Bridge Inn
imperial_bridge_inn.site: An inn half on a stone bridge and half on the bank, with lanterns strung along the span and the river passing beneath its floorboards.
imperial_bridge_inn.mystery: The river under the inn has fallen a hand's breadth every season. The innkeeper pays a 'water-tax' to a body named only 'the Ring'.
clues: a water-line scored on the pier with a hand's-width gap each year
tax receipts stamped by a ringed seal
a cellar sluice with a rusted wheel and fresh oil
imperial_bridge_inn.payoff: A water-tax seal, usable to pass as a clerk of the Ring.
imperial_bridge_inn.rumour: The river under the Bridge Inn drops every year though it rains. The keeper pays a tax nobody can name.

chorrol.name: Chorrol
chorrol.site: A town gathered under a great oak whose canopy roofs the central green, with honey-stone houses and a tiled guildhall.
chorrol.mystery: A clerk's cipher in the oak's roots lists 'sluice 1 to 40'. The Ring's records are kept in a hollow under the tree.
clues: a hollow in the oak's root scored with numbers
guild clerks who lock their drawers when a plumber enters
a pump-house with a plate stamped with a ring
chorrol.payoff: A sluice-list naming forty reservoir gates under Cyrodiil.

cheydinhal.name: Cheydinhal
cheydinhal.site: A canal-split town where the Corbolo river bisects houses, Nibenese blue tile beside Dunmer ash-grey flat roofs.
cheydinhal.mystery: Dunmer refugees say the canals were bone dry in the year they arrived and fill only when an old tax is paid. The ash-houses keep a well that tastes of iron.
clues: a canal lock with a ringed plate
a refugee well whose bucket is always cold
a canal-bank mural that shows forty gates in a ring
cheydinhal.payoff: A well-key, showing which of the forty gates is poisoned.
cheydinhal.thread_clue: refugees' ash-jars labelled with ancestors' names

bravil.name: Bravil
bravil.site: A city piled up a steep river-bay hill of leaning plank houses, stairs and rope bridges below a statue of the Lucky Old Lady.
bravil.mystery: The statue's plinth holds a sluice access that the Ring has welded shut. Bravil floods more with each season's tax.
clues: a plinth with a welded hatch
flooded cellars across the lower bay
a rope bridge hung with a ringed charm
bravil.payoff: A hatch-cutter's tool and the plan of the lowest cistern.
bravil.thread_clue: a cellar where the ledger-and-moon seal is carved in a lintel

imperial_city.name: Imperial City
imperial_city.site: Concentric rings of districts on a lake island under a white tower, with one bridge and separate walled wards.
imperial_city.mystery: The Ring of reservoirs ends beneath the Waterfront, where a private vault of the Treasury sits among Ayleid cisterns and drowned names. A sealed sewer grate opens only to a ringed seal.
clues: a sewer grate under the Waterfront stamped with a ring
a wardrobe in the Palace with a sluice-wheel inside
a lake whose level is chalked daily by clerks
imperial_city.payoff: The reservoir ledger: proof of the theft and a way to turn the Ring's water back.

khuul.name: Khuul
khuul.site: A single street of ash-grey houses on a sea cliff with a long wooden stair running down to the water and a lantern at every landing.
khuul.mystery: Every night at least one villager walks up the cliff stair asleep. The elders put slippers by the graves of those who do not return.
clues: slippers left beside empty cliff-graves
ash on stair treads in the shape of bare feet
a lantern on every landing that is kept burning against sleep
khuul.payoff: A child's chalk map marking the sleepers' route up the mountain.
khuul.rumour: In Khuul, someone walks the cliff stair asleep every night. The elders leave the lanterns lit and do not wake them.

ald_velothi.name: Ald Velothi
ald_velothi.site: A harbour village of one temple and many boat-houses along a bay where the water goes grey from fallen ash.
ald_velothi.mystery: The village's boats are drawn up in a ring and none sails by night; the dreamers wade out and fall asleep in the water, and are found at dawn standing in a line, facing inland.
clues: boats drawn up in a ring at the tide line
a line of wet footprints leading into the sea and out again
a temple wall scratched with a count that stops at forty
ald_velothi.payoff: The temple's night-watch roster, a map of the sleepers' wading line.
ald_velothi.rumour: Ald Velothi hasn't put a boat out at night in months. They say the dreamers wade into the bay and stand there till dawn.

urshilaku_camp.name: Urshilaku Camp
urshilaku_camp.site: An Ashlander camp of yurts under hide, a wise woman's fire in the centre, and sleeping-mats ringed in ash-cord.
urshilaku_camp.mystery: The Ashlanders say the dreaming has a fire in its heart. The wise woman keeps a cord of knots, one for each sleeper taken, and says the ghostfence is thinning in the shape of a doorway.
clues: knotted cords hung from every yurt-pole
a fire that burns without smoke
a sleeping-mat laid at the camp's edge facing the mountain
urshilaku_camp.payoff: A dream-lantern: a ward-light that stops a sleeper's walk.
urshilaku_camp.rumour: The Urshilaku wise woman has been saying the ash is awake and has been for a year. The Temple laughs. The sleepers do not.

ghostfence_morrowind.name: Ghostfence
ghostfence_morrowind.site: A long wall of shimmering ghost-light enclosing the mountain, broken at gate-posts and humming at a pitch just below hearing.
ghostfence_morrowind.mystery: A section of the fence has thinned into the shape of a person walking. The gap moves up the slope an inch a night, and the sleepers' footprints line up with it.
clues: a shimmer in the fence shaped like a walking figure
gate-posts wrapped in tied ribbons
sleepers' slippers piled neatly at the fence line
ghostfence_morrowind.payoff: A shard of ghostfence light that opens the rear door of an ash sanctum.
ghostfence_morrowind.rumour: The ghostfence has a gap you can see only at dusk, shaped like a person. It moves.
ghostfence_morrowind.thread_clue: an ash-urn pinned with a map of prevailing winds

missamsi.name: Missamsi
missamsi.site: A corrupted ashland sanctum of blighted stone and red crystal growths, descending through ash-choked halls to a pulsing chamber.
missamsi.mystery: A remnant of dream-cultists still feeds the ash its 'audience'. They believe they will wake something kindly. They do not know the ash only wants company.
clues: beds of ash arranged in rows in the lowest hall
red crystal that grows toward sleepers' hands
a mural of figures walking uphill with closed eyes
missamsi.payoff: A crystal that records a sleeper's dream, and a key to the Kogoruhn amphitheatre.
missamsi.rumour: Something under Missamsi is still keeping a bed warm. Stay out of the ash after dusk.

kogoruhn.name: Kogoruhn
kogoruhn.site: A blasted ash-fortress at the foot of the mountain, with broken keeps half-buried in drifts and a collapsed amphitheatre.
kogoruhn.mystery: The amphitheatre is the sleepers' destination. They stand in tiers on the ash and watch a performance only they can see. A performer's mask hangs on the stage.
clues: an amphitheatre with ash-seats facing an empty stage
a mask hung on a peg with eye-slots worn smooth
drifts shaped like people with their heads bowed
kogoruhn.payoff: The performer's mask: a one-use item that lets the wearer be seen by the dreamers.
kogoruhn.rumour: At Kogoruhn the ash seats are full of sleepers. They don't turn their heads when you walk through.

red_mountain.name: Red Mountain
red_mountain.site: A bruised volcano whose ash plume shades the sky, with a glowing crown and a ring of broken wall.
red_mountain.mystery: At the crater rim, ash lies in rows like beds, and the dreamer's seat is carved into the lip facing inward. Whoever sits there is heard.
clues: rows of ash-beds along the crater rim
a carved seat on the lip facing inward
a plume that bends toward the watchers
red_mountain.payoff: The dreamer's seat's rest: a unique ash-ward that quiets the Ashlands for a season.
red_mountain.thread_clue: ash that drifts against the wind toward a distant canal

seyda_neen.name: Seyda Neen
seyda_neen.site: A tiny customs-house port at a lagoon edge, with a silt-strider stop, a pier and a lighthouse with a ledger-room.
seyda_neen.mystery: The customs ledger counts more pilgrims landed than ever sail home, a difference of eleven hundred this year. The clerk has begun writing the difference in the margin in red.
clues: a customs ledger with a red margin column
a pier with sets of luggage nobody collects
a customs seal cracked and glued back
seyda_neen.payoff: The red-margin ledger, proof of the missing pilgrims.
seyda_neen.rumour: The Seyda Neen clerk says there are more pilgrims coming in than going out. She has stopped opening the post.

pelagiad.name: Pelagiad
pelagiad.site: A fortified hill village with a half-built fort and a granary where the roads from the pier all meet.
pelagiad.mystery: Pilgrims are fed at the granary and sent in groups at night along the old road. The fort's captain has stopped asking where.
clues: pilgrim bundles stacked in the granary loft
a road marked with chalk crescents at every milestone
a fort gate left unbarred by order
pelagiad.payoff: A road-pass chalked on a roof tile, valid at the next shrine field.
pelagiad.rumour: Every night the pilgrims leave the Pelagiad granary in a quiet line. The captain locks his door.

fields_of_kummu.name: Fields of Kummu
fields_of_kummu.site: A green flat of old standing shrines in ash grass, each carved with a face that looks toward the lagoon.
fields_of_kummu.mystery: The shrine faces each hold a pilgrim's token, deposited and never collected. A dozen shrines are freshly tended by clerks in plain robes.
clues: tokens in niches in every shrine face
grass trampled in a path to the lagoon edge
a clerk's desk set up beside a shrine, deserted
fields_of_kummu.payoff: A shrine-token that opens a sunken door in Ald Sotha.
fields_of_kummu.rumour: The Kummu shrines are tended by clerks nobody has met. They keep a ledger of tokens left and tokens never taken.

ald_sotha.name: Ald Sotha
ald_sotha.site: A huge ancient Velothi shrine fortress with dusky green stone, great doors and a sunken lower temple of a long-silent god.
ald_sotha.mystery: The lower temple is a filing room: drawer upon drawer of tokens and names, and a stair that descends under the water toward the lagoon.
clues: drawers of tokens along every wall of the lower hall
a stair that runs straight into dark water
a door whose lock is worked with a shrine-token
ald_sotha.payoff: A filing-room key and a map of the stair under the lagoon.
ald_sotha.rumour: Ald Sotha's lower rooms flood and drain on a schedule. Some say a clerk's bell rings down there.

vivecs_antlers.name: Vivec's Antlers
vivecs_antlers.site: Two giant antlered peaks over the Stonefalls coast, one broken, with a pilgrims' ladder rungs worn smooth.
vivecs_antlers.mystery: The broken antler's rungs end in a sealed door half-way up. The pilgrims who climb it are not seen coming down.
clues: a ladder with rungs worn glassy at the broken antler
a door sealed in blue wax halfway up
pilgrim shoes left in a line at the base
vivecs_antlers.payoff: A wax-seal stamp that unseals the pilgrims' door.
vivecs_antlers.rumour: The pilgrims' ladder on the broken antler goes up and the pilgrims go up and I have never seen one come down.

ebonheart.name: Ebonheart
ebonheart.site: An old Imperial fortress-port on the Stonefalls coast, black-walled and salt-stained, with a star-shaped castle on a river island.
ebonheart.mystery: A line in the Imperial accounts pays a stipend for 'the seventh quiet', and the Imperial factor is scared of it. The ledger was kept by the East Empire Company.
clues: a stipend line for 'the seventh quiet' in the factor's books
star-fort cellars with a sealed lagoon-door
crates marked for Vivec that never left the quay
ebonheart.payoff: The factor's sealed stipend ledger, naming the canton's payers.

vivec.name: Vivec City
vivec.site: Six pyramidal cantons standing in water, joined by long arched bridges, with the Palace as a stepped ziggurat at the centre.
vivec.mystery: A seventh canton lies beneath the lagoon: lamplit offices where the pilgrims who never left are filed, fed and kept patient by Temple clerks.
clues: a seventh door in the harbour wall nobody uses
a canton bridge that stops at the water
a clerk's bell that rings below the lagoon
vivec.payoff: A roll of the quiet canton's filed names, and a sealed permit for any who wish to leave.

hla_oad.name: Hla Oad
hla_oad.site: A tidal fishing village of smoke-racks where the tide leaves mudflats scattered with brass glints.
hla_oad.mystery: Fishermen haul brass cogs and tiny levers from the flats and sell them to one buyer who pays triple for those carrying a thumb-print.
clues: urns full of small brass cogs
smoke-racks hung with brass chains alongside fish
a trader's tent with a scale and a stamped receipt-book
hla_oad.payoff: The buyer's receipt-book, naming a Balmora collector.
hla_oad.rumour: The Hla Oad mudflats give up brass at every ebb. A trader pays triple if it has a little thumb-print.

gnaar_mok.name: Gnaar Mok
gnaar_mok.site: A muddy swamp town raised on stilts with a mangrove market and a landing for silt striders.
gnaar_mok.mystery: The stilt market's most expensive stall sells nothing, only receipts for brass; the stall-keeper is a courier for a master in Balmora. A single stilt-house is kept sealed and ticks.
clues: a stall that sells no goods and only issues receipts
a stilt-house door that ticks softly in the night
mangrove roots wired with brass chains
gnaar_mok.payoff: A courier's token that opens a Balmora cellar door.
gnaar_mok.rumour: A stall in the Gnaar Mok market sells receipts and nothing else. Someone's always buying.
gnaar_mok.thread_clue: a stilt-house whose floor is a hatch with a ledger on its lid

balmora.name: Balmora
balmora.site: A river town on both banks of the Odai, with low spreading Hlaalu houses on terraces and a giant silt strider docked at the south side.
balmora.mystery: A Hlaalu collector's cellar holds a brass guest in pieces, assembled by night. He calls it 'the Attendant' and tells guests it is a sculpture.
clues: a cellar door with a thumb-print plate
brass dust on the stair of a council-house
a silt strider laden with crates marked 'sculpture'
balmora.payoff: A coil spring, the Attendant's missing power piece.
balmora.thread_clue: a silt-strider cargo-hold stamped with a ledger

rkuldumz_spire.name: Rkuldumz Spire
rkuldumz_spire.site: A tall brass-pipe tower on a rock island off the Telvannis coast, whose top vents steam at fixed hours.
rkuldumz_spire.mystery: The spire is a radio of sorts, calling the Attendant's parts together. Its vents steam at the same hour the cogs are found on the flats.
clues: steam venting at a fixed hour each tide
pipework wrapped in dead fishing nets
a boat landing with brass-cog barnacles
rkuldumz_spire.payoff: A tuning rod that silences the spire's call.
rkuldumz_spire.rumour: Rkuldumz steams once at the turn of every tide and the brass glints on the mud shift on the hour.
rkuldumz_spire.thread_clue: a summit dial whose hand is a finger's breadth from the cross

halls_of_fabrication.name: Halls of Fabrication
halls_of_fabrication.site: A conveyor-and-forge hall with long assembly lines of half-built animunculi and a forge-pit finale, hammer sounds echoing in foundry glow.
halls_of_fabrication.mystery: The assembly lines have been restarted by something. The half-built figures are all missing the same part, the one the collector is gathering.
clues: assembly-line slots empty at the same station
a forge-pit glowing beyond all reason
a conveyor stamped with a thumb-print mould
halls_of_fabrication.payoff: A mould of the Attendant's thumb, which lets any animunculus accept the wearer as a master.
halls_of_fabrication.rumour: Hammer-sounds in the Halls of Fabrication again. The machines are making something, but they never finish.
halls_of_fabrication.thread_clue: a bronze dial behind a conveyor, its hand one tick from the cross

arkngthand.name: Arkngthand
arkngthand.site: A Dwemer city-hall of cranking bronze with giant gear-halls, steam vents and a centrifuge chamber at the core.
arkngthand.mystery: The centrifuge chamber holds the Attendant's seat. The assembled guest knelt there and asked, in a voice of struck copper, whether its makers will return.
clues: a bronze seat worn smooth by a single occupant
a centrifuge turning one revolution an hour
a ledger plate with a single tick-mark
arkngthand.payoff: A Dwemer command-rod, a unique tool of Brass that sets a construct free.
arkngthand.rumour: Arkngthand still turns, one revolution an hour. Locals say there is someone in the middle of it, waiting.
arkngthand.thread_clue: a dial plate set beside the centrifuge seat

tel_branora.name: Tel Branora
tel_branora.site: A single huge mushroom tower on a lagoon, with a master and his servants and a tidal causeway that floods twice a day.
tel_branora.mystery: The master has been dead for years. The tower's bequests are signed by him every season, in a hand that has gone slightly wrong.
clues: bequests dated after the master's death
a signature that drifts leftward year on year
servants who set the master's place at every meal
tel_branora.payoff: A bequest-seal that lets a bearer attend the quiet vote in Mournhold.
tel_branora.rumour: The master of Tel Branora has been dead for six years. His letters still arrive every season.

molag_mar.name: Molag Mar
molag_mar.site: A town cut into a sea cliff with a lava-lit grotto at its heart, houses balanced on ledges above a glowing channel and a temple canton reached by long stairs.
molag_mar.mystery: The grotto's lava channel carries a dead man's ash urn each night down to the sea, unsigned. The channel-keepers say there is nowhere left to bury them.
clues: urns sliding down the lava channel at night
a grotto wall of unmarked memorial plaques
ash stairs where each step bears a different family sigil
molag_mar.payoff: A memorial plaque with a seat number: the dead's voting seat.
molag_mar.rumour: The urns come down the lava channel at Molag Mar every night. No one will say who throws them.
molag_mar.thread_clue: a lava-cascade that cools and stills at the hush hour

necrom.name: Necrom
necrom.site: A city of the dead and the living, with ancestral tomb-houses in terraced rows climbing a hillside and lantern-lined processional avenues.
necrom.mystery: Tomb-houses are emptying: the ancestors walk out at dusk in a line for Mournhold. Temple clerks keep minutes of what they vote on.
clues: tomb doors left ajar at dusk
a clerk's desk with minute-books in the tomb-house cellars
lanterns trimmed for a procession that nobody sees
necrom.payoff: A minute-book of the quiet vote, with the seats and who sits in them.

sadrith_mora.name: Sadrith Mora
sadrith_mora.site: A cluster of giant fungal towers on a lagoon island, each noble's tower a different cap colour, joined by rope footbridges.
sadrith_mora.mystery: The towers each keep a seat in the quiet vote. The masters are not quite alive, and a shadow-secretary collects their ballots by lamp at midnight.
clues: tower windows lit at midnight in a rotating order
a shadow-secretary who is nobody's servant
spore-lamps burning on the empty chairs
sadrith_mora.payoff: A ballot, which shows the quiet vote's current question.

aldruhn.name: Ald'ruhn
aldruhn.site: A fortress-town built inside and along a monstrous crab shell with ribs forming gate arches and long halls.
aldruhn.mystery: The Redoran council hall holds a chair no one is allowed to sit in, with a cushion that is always warm. The council's votes tally forty-one, and there are forty living members.
clues: a chair under dust sheets that is always warm
votes tallied at forty-one
a gate arch whose rib is carved with a seat number
aldruhn.payoff: The forty-first seat's summons, an invitation to the lower council.

mournhold.name: Mournhold
mournhold.site: A walled white-and-gold citadel of domed Temple, palace and great plaza, with the Great Bazaar as an enclosed arcade.
mournhold.mystery: A grating under the Temple's plaza opens on the lightless city below, where a long table sits set for forty. The Temple has paved the plaza over it twice.
clues: a grating under the plaza that exhales cold
pavers' marks on stones laid over the grating twice
a bell below ground that rings at midnight
mournhold.payoff: A pavers' key to the lower grating.

old_mournhold.name: Old Mournhold
old_mournhold.site: The sunken twin of Mournhold: the same plazas lying one level down, lightless, with collapsed arcades and a flooded bazaar.
old_mournhold.mystery: A mirror-hall in the lower Temple holds a table set for forty. The dead sit in it, and vote. Their speaker has begun to say 'we' for the living.
clues: a table in a mirror-hall set for forty
mirrors in which the living do not appear
a gavel that rings on its own at the hour
old_mournhold.payoff: The Quiet Vote's gavel: a unique relic that can adjourn the dead's council.
old_mournhold.rumour: Under Mournhold's plaza a table is set for forty. Those who've seen it won't say who sat there.

old_attius_farm.name: Old Attius Farm
old_attius_farm.site: A farm in the ash south of Raven Rock, with rows of ash-yams on volcanic dirt and a storage shed with empty seed-jars.
old_attius_farm.mystery: The Attius family's seed-jars are labelled 'third of three' in a careful hand that is not theirs. The farm is a single link in an old botanist's trail.
clues: seed-jars labelled in an Imperial hand
yam rows planted in a surveyor's straight lines
a scarecrow wearing a botanist's field-coat
old_attius_farm.payoff: The third of three: a seed-bank key stamp.

raven_rock.name: Raven Rock
raven_rock.site: A mining colony behind a hastily built stone bulwark, with ebony-spoil heaps, a headframe over the shaft and Redoran long-houses.
raven_rock.mystery: The bulwark's cornerstone hides the second third of the map. The mine foreman says the first settlers were not miners but a botanical survey.
clues: a cornerstone chiselled with a plant glyph
mine-shaft timbers stamped with a survey seal
a ledger-room where a page is cut out
raven_rock.payoff: The second third of the seed-bank map.
raven_rock.thread_clue: grey ash-drifts that settle only on the north side of the bulwark

brodir_grove.name: Brodir Grove
brodir_grove.site: A grove of ancient trees in the ash wastes, one of the few green places left, whose trunks spiral in unison toward the north.
brodir_grove.mystery: The trees' spirals point to the temple under the mountain. The settlers' survey marked each spiral as a bearing.
clues: trunks spiralling in the same direction
survey stakes still bearing fading ribbons
a stone marker in the roots with a glyph for 'seed'
brodir_grove.payoff: The grove's bearing, the last third of the map.
brodir_grove.thread_clue: grove-roots that whisper where ash has settled

fort_frostmoth.name: Fort Frostmoth
fort_frostmoth.site: A broken Imperial fort in a snowfield, with a square curtain wall, a frozen moat and a tower with a blue lantern.
fort_frostmoth.mystery: The garrison guarded a survey party and were ordered to say nothing. Their cellar holds crates of seed-sacks sealed in wax.
clues: wax-sealed crates in the fort cellar
a blue lantern that points inland
a garrison log with its last page torn
fort_frostmoth.payoff: A sealed crate of seed-sacks that unlocks the greenhouse door.

ashfallow_citadel.name: Ashfallow Citadel
ashfallow_citadel.site: A walled Telvanni citadel in the ash wastes with ruined wings and a ward-ring, held by a renegade wizard.
ashfallow_citadel.mystery: The renegade wizard wants the seed-bank as a breeding stock for fungal crops. He has a third of the key, taken from a surveyor's corpse.
clues: a surveyor's skeleton on the ward-ring
fungal beds of failed grain
a ledger of hybrid crops, all labelled 'incomplete'
ashfallow_citadel.payoff: The surveyor's key, which opens the temple cellar.

tel_mithryn.name: Tel Mithryn
tel_mithryn.site: A massive mushroom tower on an ash-flat wrapped in spore-stairs with a small garden of glowing fungi.
tel_mithryn.mystery: The tower's master has already tried a path to the seed-bank and failed: his garden's glowing fungi are descendants of what he took. The master wants a witness.
clues: glowing fungi in rows labelled with failed species
a master's workbook of crop crosses
a boat-shaped stable full of seed-barrels
tel_mithryn.payoff: A master's workbook that shows which seeds the cellar will hold.

temple_of_miraak.name: Temple of Miraak
temple_of_miraak.site: A Dragon Priest's mountain temple, frost-sealed, with a long stair, grand chambers and a sunken inner sanctum where the walls move like ink.
temple_of_miraak.mystery: The cellar of the temple's lowest nave is the seed-bank. A sealing ward keeps it fresh, and a warden of grown green guards it from anyone who tries to take the jars.
clues: jars lined on shelves behind a ward of ink-black stone
roots that grow only inside the lowest nave
a stair worn by botanists' boots, older than the ward
temple_of_miraak.payoff: A sealed jar of unblighted seed: a unique that grows safe crops in ashland.

abandoned_lodge.name: Abandoned Lodge
abandoned_lodge.site: A hunting lodge below Hvitkald Peak with its door hanging open, a pot still hanging over cold coals and a bone flute in a cloak on the porch.
abandoned_lodge.mystery: The hunter went to ask the sixth All-Maker stone why it had gone quiet. His flute and note remain; he does not.
clues: a bone flute in a folded cloak
a note scratched on the porch rail
a larder untouched, with meat gone cold under its cloth
abandoned_lodge.payoff: The hunter's flute: a ceremonial instrument that wakes a stone.

hvitkald_peak.name: Hvitkald Peak
hvitkald_peak.site: A conical peak with a crown of ice, streaked with ash on its flanks, with a hunters' cairn at the summit.
hvitkald_peak.mystery: The cairn holds the first of the island's five answers: a note in the wind. The sixth is missing from the peak, and the cairn-keepers' count stops at five.
clues: a cairn with five notched stones and one blank
ash stripes on the summit ice
wind that carries a single plucked note
hvitkald_peak.payoff: The first answer: a note that harmonises with the flute.
hvitkald_peak.thread_clue: a frozen rib on the summit with a numbered tag

stalhrim_source.name: Stalhrim Source
stalhrim_source.site: A frozen crack of blue-white glow in a basin, the ice itself humming at a pitch just below hearing.
stalhrim_source.mystery: The stalhrim hums the second answer. The Skaal guard it not because it is valuable but because it is the only stone in the island that sings back.
clues: ice that hums when a flute is held to it
Skaal guards who tie wool over the crack at night
frost-rime in the shape of a half-open hand
stalhrim_source.payoff: The second answer, a stalhrim shard that rings true.
stalhrim_source.thread_clue: a stalhrim hum that drops a tone at the hush hour

allmaker_water_stone.name: All-Maker Water Stone
allmaker_water_stone.site: One of six standing stones of the All-Maker, raised by the Skaal on the island's west shore, wet with spray.
allmaker_water_stone.mystery: The water stone answers but with a weeping note. Alone of the six it grieves, and the Skaal pretend not to hear.
clues: wet stone that does not dry in sun
offerings of fish-bone left with fresh flowers
a hollow beside it in the shape of a sitting person
allmaker_water_stone.payoff: The third answer: a weeping note that opens the barrow door.

skaal_village.name: Skaal Village
skaal_village.site: A ring of low hide-and-bone houses around a central stone circle and fire, with drying racks and hanging totems.
skaal_village.mystery: The elder knows the sixth stone is mute and has told no one. The village sings only five verses at the winter fire, and the children have begun to hum the sixth.
clues: a sixth, blank carving on the circle's stone
children's songs with a gap where the sixth verse sits
an elder's door closed on the winter fire
skaal_village.payoff: The elder's confession and the sixth verse's first line.

altar_of_thrond.name: Altar of Thrond
altar_of_thrond.site: A weathered stone altar between the mountain and the temple, older than the Skaal, ringed by carved posts with a view of the island.
altar_of_thrond.mystery: The altar's posts form a tally of verses. Five are weathered smooth, the sixth was deliberately defaced. The scrape is recent.
clues: a sixth post defaced with fresh tool marks
offerings of antler and honey, unclaimed
a worn path leading east toward the barrow
altar_of_thrond.payoff: A rubbing of the defaced verse and a map of the barrow's mural wall.

gyldenhul_barrow.name: Gyldenhul Barrow
gyldenhul_barrow.site: A large Nordic barrow on the east shore with a tiered nave and a glowing mural of a long-dead king.
gyldenhul_barrow.mystery: The mural's king is the first Skaal chief who promised the island silence. The lost hunter is painted into its edge, still singing the sixth verse.
clues: a mural with a figure painted into its border
a tiered nave echoing with a hummed note
fresh paint where the sixth verse was overwritten
gyldenhul_barrow.payoff: The sixth verse, restoring the stone and the island's voice.
gyldenhul_barrow.thread_clue: a mural king with one finger scraped away

ramshackle_trading_post.name: Ramshackle Trading Post
ramshackle_trading_post.site: A wind-battered trading post on the road between Kagrumez and the coast, shacks around a single stove.
ramshackle_trading_post.mystery: The Orc trader buys anything but will not sell the stove-lid, which bears the last of four sets of charts from a lost ship.
clues: a stove-lid stamped with a ship's-wheel
a drawer of oiled bone charts under the trader's cot
crates marked with a wrecked ship's crest
ramshackle_trading_post.payoff: Chart Four: the compass-line to the Dwemer cold-engine.

bujolds_retreat.name: Bujold's Retreat
bujolds_retreat.site: A Nord homestead on the east coast abandoned by the family who built it, occupied by reavers.
bujolds_retreat.mystery: The reavers are the last of Haknir's crew, who vowed never to sail again. They keep Chart Three nailed beneath a table.
clues: a table with a chart pinned underneath
reaver tallies of ships lost
a hearth with a ship's name burnt into the beam
bujolds_retreat.payoff: Chart Three, with a note of the wreck's last position.

haknirs_shoal.name: Haknir's Shoal
haknirs_shoal.site: The rotting wreck of a ship's ribs caught on rocks in surf on the north shore.
haknirs_shoal.mystery: Chart Two was sealed in the ship's bow. The crew swore not to sail; the ship went anyway, steered by a thing in the hold.
clues: a ship's ribs with a sealed bow-chest
a steering oar tied off at a heading
barnacle-encrusted cold-engine vanes in the bilge
haknirs_shoal.payoff: Chart Two and a vane from the cold-engine.
haknirs_shoal.thread_clue: a bow-chest holding a salt-stained page with a tide-glyph

thirsk_mead_hall.name: Thirsk Mead Hall
thirsk_mead_hall.site: One immense hall in a walled compound with whale-rib arches, a trophy yard and a fenced boar run.
thirsk_mead_hall.mystery: The skald sings Haknir's saga with a verse that is wrong on purpose, naming the last chart's hiding place. No one realised it was a clue.
clues: a whale-rib arch carved with a ship and a snowflake
a skald who lingers on one verse
a trophy shield stamped with a wheel
thirsk_mead_hall.payoff: Chart One: tucked behind the trophy shield.

kagrumez.name: Kagrumez
kagrumez.site: A Dwemer observatory on a ridge with an open sky-dome room, star-maps and a long gantry over a pit.
kagrumez.mystery: The star-maps are set to a night that has not happened yet, the night the cold-engine will wake. The ridge's resonance chambers hum a lower note.
clues: star-maps set to a future night
a gantry with a worn guide-rail
a resonance chamber whose frost creeps in one direction
kagrumez.payoff: A star-map key aligned to the engine's awakening.
kagrumez.thread_clue: a dial in the star-dome that ticks in time with the other seven

nchardak.name: Nchardak
nchardak.site: A Dwemer city half sunk in ice with a crystalline roof, flooded lower levels and a steam-lift.
nchardak.mystery: The ice here is a coolant. The giant's throne, a day's march away, is the outlet of the same engine. Break the coolant and the island thaws.
clues: coolant pipes frosted white
a lift whose cage is carved with the engine's mark
a flooded hall with a gauge reading 'cold'
nchardak.payoff: A pressure valve that can open or close the engine.
nchardak.thread_clue: a dial iced over but its hand still moving

castle_karstaag_ruins.name: Castle Karstaag
castle_karstaag_ruins.site: A giant's frozen castle, big-scale rooms with towering doors, a throne of ice and frozen warriors.
castle_karstaag_ruins.mystery: The throne is the engine's outlet. Something took up Karstaag's seat after him and has been warming its hands on the ice.
clues: a throne that radiates cold
frozen giant-warriors turned toward it
engine vanes half-sunk in the throne's base
castle_karstaag_ruins.payoff: The engine's vane: a unique frost-relic that sets the island's winter.

aldhaven_harbor.name: Aldhaven Harbor
aldhaven_harbor.site: A small harbour on the Iliac Bay's shore with a heavy chain across the mouth and a tidal slip for night barges.
aldhaven_harbor.mystery: A barge leaves the chain gate every ninth night with a manifest of 'stone dust, chisels, one priest' and returns lighter. Nobody has seen the priest come back.
clues: chisel dust in the slip's wet planks
a chain-keeper's log with the same entry every ninth night
a priest's stole snagged on a mooring ring
aldhaven_harbor.payoff: A chain-gate pass that lets the barge be followed to the tomb.
aldhaven_harbor.rumour: A barge with no cargo but dust slips out of Aldhaven every ninth night and comes back lighter.

glenpoint.name: Glenpoint
glenpoint.site: A small walled port on a headland with a single gate, a beacon keep and houses crowded to the end of the quay.
glenpoint.mystery: The beacon is lit on the barge's nights though no ship is expected. A chisel-sharpening wheel runs in a boat-shed all night.
clues: a beacon lit at odd hours
a boat-shed wheel throwing sparks past midnight
masons' aprons stacked wet on the quay
glenpoint.payoff: A mason's apron with a Wayrest guild-seal sewn in.
glenpoint.rumour: The beacon at Glenpoint is lit on nights no ship is expected, and a grinding wheel runs in the boat-shed until dawn.

wayrest.name: Wayrest
wayrest.site: A harbour capital in a bay with a castle on a rock spur, a chain-boom across the harbour and guild streets rising in a bowl.
wayrest.mystery: The masons' guild is paid by the crown to maintain the royal archives, and a clerk's accounts show payments to 'the Quiet Chisel' from three courts.
clues: a payment line to 'the Quiet Chisel'
masons' guildhall doors shut at the ninth bell
a clerk's desk with a drawer lined in stone dust
wayrest.payoff: The Quiet Chisel's payment list, with three royal seals.

daggerfall.name: Daggerfall
daggerfall.site: A fortified river-mouth town with a castle on an island linked by two stone bridges and tall houses over the water.
daggerfall.mystery: The court archives were closed to scholars last year. A single scribe argues in the margins of the royal genealogy that there are eight kings, not seven.
clues: a scholar's marginal note: 'eight, not seven'
archive doors sealed with fresh wax
a scribe who keeps a counting-rod on his belt
daggerfall.payoff: The scribe's marginal copy of the genealogy.

camlorn.name: Camlorn
camlorn.site: A hill-top city of cream stone and spiky slate roofs with many spires and a cathedral of flying buttresses.
camlorn.mystery: The cathedral's bell-keeper retired in tears after a mason asked to 'tidy' the lower chapel's inscription. The chapel is now locked.
clues: a lower chapel inscription half-chiselled
a bell-keeper's farewell letter pinned to the door
mason's marks in three different guild hands
camlorn.payoff: The cathedral's original inscription, copied before the chisel came.

cath_bedraud.name: Cath Bedraud
cath_bedraud.site: A knight's crypt under a ruined chapel with long vaulted aisles of effigies, a bone-lined crypt and a hollow font.
cath_bedraud.mystery: One effigy in the long aisle is a king, not a knight, and was carved by hand after the others. Its name has been struck out and refilled with plaster.
clues: an effigy with a crown among knights
plaster in the cut where a name once was
a font that fills with chisel dust
cath_bedraud.payoff: The plaster-cast of the eighth king's name.
cath_bedraud.rumour: In Cath Bedraud the knights' stone faces all look one way: toward a niche that has been plastered shut.

tomb_of_lost_kings.name: Tomb of Lost Kings
tomb_of_lost_kings.site: A dynasty's necropolis with named sarcophagi and a family tree carved on the great wall, each room one king.
tomb_of_lost_kings.mystery: There are seven king-rooms and a sealed eighth, its door already half-recarved into wall. The master-mason works inside, erasing the last name.
clues: a family tree with a branch recently planed away
a king-room whose door is now a wall
tools laid neatly in a sarcophagus
tomb_of_lost_kings.payoff: A unique charcoal rubbing of the eighth king's name and his legitimate heirs' line.
tomb_of_lost_kings.rumour: The Tomb of Lost Kings has an eighth door that some days is there and some days is not.
tomb_of_lost_kings.thread_clue: a royal seal cut in two, the other half missing

the_lonely_lantern.name: The Lonely Lantern
the_lonely_lantern.site: A one-lamp inn on a moor in the fog, with a single lantern in the window and a table laid for a guest.
the_lonely_lantern.mystery: Every guest who stayed the night is gone by morning, leaving a cream-coloured card on the table. The innkeeper counts them and says she will be next.
clues: cream cards stacked in a jar
one place set at the table with no chair
a lantern that burns lavender at midnight
the_lonely_lantern.payoff: A card whose invitation can be answered.
the_lonely_lantern.rumour: The Lonely Lantern keeps its one lamp lit all night. Guests who sleep there leave a card and no footprints.

moiras_hope.name: Moira's Hope
moiras_hope.site: A tiny shrine hamlet on a moor-edge, with a single prayer-stone ringed in candle-ends and a bell that does not ring.
moiras_hope.mystery: The villagers say yes to the invitations out of grief, one at a time. The shrine keeps their candle-ends in a box with the cards.
clues: candle-ends in a box labelled with names
a bell with its clapper tied
cream cards tucked into the prayer-stone
moiras_hope.payoff: A candle-end that lets the bearer keep their name against the fog.
moiras_hope.rumour: At Moira's Hope the villagers light a candle for each who says yes to the fog.

northpoint.name: Northpoint
northpoint.site: A rock-bound northern port on a moor with houses clinging to a sea cliff, stairs down to the quay and a squat lighthouse in the mist.
northpoint.mystery: The lighthouse keeper turns the lamp off at the party's hour, because ships that keep their bearings do not accept invitations.
clues: a lighthouse dark at the fog hour
ships moored by moor-lanterns in a ring
a harbour-master with a silver bell round his neck
northpoint.payoff: A silver ward-bell that rings a warning against fog-voices.
northpoint.rumour: The lighthouse at Northpoint is dark at the fog hour, by order of the harbour-master, who wears a small silver bell round his neck.

shornhelm.name: Shornhelm
shornhelm.site: The black-roofed capital of Rivenspire, a city of fog, feuding houses and a heavy red keep in a grid-planned wall.
shornhelm.mystery: The feuding houses sent heirs to the party to settle old debts. None returned. The keep's cellars hold a guest-book, signed with plum ink.
clues: a guest-book signed in plum ink
a house's mourning flags in every colour
heirs' empty seats at a council table
shornhelm.payoff: The guest-book, naming who sold the guest list.

doomcrag.name: Doomcrag
doomcrag.site: A black spire on a crag with spiral wards, a library of bound books and a roof with a storm engine.
doomcrag.mystery: The necromancer sold the guest list to the Host in exchange for a tome. He keeps a copy to know who is going to disappear next.
clues: a library with a second ledger of 'next invitees'
a storm engine whose dial reads 'fog'
a desk with a plum-inked quill
doomcrag.payoff: The second ledger and a door-key to the demesne.
doomcrag.rumour: The Doomcrag library has a ledger of names, and the necromancer reads it every night.

sanguines_demesne.name: Sanguine's Demesne
sanguines_demesne.site: A realm-pocket of red velvet with banqueting halls, endless mirror corridors and a throne of bones where the party has gone on too long.
sanguines_demesne.mystery: The guests are not unhappy. They are happy and cannot leave. The Host wants a single witness to sign the register, so that the party can formally end and begin again.
clues: a long table with plates that steam
mirror corridors that show a different guest each pass
a register on a bone lectern waiting for a signature
sanguines_demesne.payoff: The register, a unique that frees a named guest from the party.
sanguines_demesne.rumour: The invitations say the supper is held in a demesne of red velvet, where no one is unhappy and no one remembers the way home.

morkul_stronghold_high_rock.name: Morkul Stronghold
morkul_stronghold_high_rock.site: A small Orc palisade in the Wrothgarian foothills with forges roaring and a hide-covered stone at its gate.
morkul_stronghold_high_rock.mystery: A name is carved at the gate each dusk by no hand, with a date nine days ahead. The smith covers it with a hide so the stronghold will not see.
clues: a hide over a stone with a fresh name
a smith's tally of who is carved this season
a palisade post with one more notch every night
morkul_stronghold_high_rock.payoff: A dusk-carved name that the smith dare not read aloud.
morkul_stronghold_high_rock.rumour: At Morkul they carve no name on the stone, and yet one appears each dusk. The smith won't speak of it.

paragons_remembrance.name: Paragon's Remembrance
paragons_remembrance.site: A tall memorial column of names, with a flat processional ground before it and a bowl for offerings.
paragons_remembrance.mystery: The column's lowest names are new and the stonemason denies cutting them. Several have already come true.
clues: new names on the lowest tier, still pale
a bowl of offerings left to the nameless
chisel marks that do not match any tool
paragons_remembrance.payoff: A rubbing of the newest names, a list of who is next.
paragons_remembrance.rumour: The Paragon's column shows names of Orcs who are still alive, and they have started to die in that order.

wrothgarian_mountains.name: Wrothgarian Mountains
wrothgarian_mountains.site: A broken ridge where the sky is a permanent dusk and sharp peaks throw shadows that never change.
wrothgarian_mountains.mystery: A shadow on the ridge falls toward the old city at a time when the sun is on the other side. The shadow's edge is a name.
clues: a shadow pointing the wrong direction
a cairn of broken hammers
dusk that holds on the ridge at noon
wrothgarian_mountains.payoff: The shadow's bearing: a straight line down to the old forge.
wrothgarian_mountains.rumour: At noon the shadows on the Wrothgarian ridge fall the wrong way, and the sky there is the colour of permanent dusk.

orsinium.name: Orsinium
orsinium.site: A stepped fortress-city on a mountain flank where each ring is a separate bastion of black stone and forge pits roar.
orsinium.mystery: The city's founders dug the new foundations into the old, and the old forge answers at night: hammer-blows heard from under the Chief's hall.
clues: hammer-blows from under the foundation at night
a forge-pit with an unlit coal that is warm
stone steps leading down behind a sealed door

old_orsinium.name: Old Orsinium
old_orsinium.site: The first Orc city, buried, with huge sloping halls in blackened stone, tilted streets, a trophy-ringed throne and a collapsed forge.
old_orsinium.mystery: A smith-spirit hammers names onto the anvil and cannot stop. Each hammer-blow is a name for the column above. It needs someone to take the hammer from its hand.
clues: an anvil covered in freshly cut names
a spectral hammer rising and falling
a throne ringed by trophies of nobody known
old_orsinium.payoff: The unwritten hammer: a unique relic that unwrites a carved name.
old_orsinium.rumour: In Old Orsinium a hammer rings against an anvil with no smith, and it is carving something.
old_orsinium.thread_clue: an anvil with a ring-shaped scorch in its face

koeglin_village.name: Koeglin Village
koeglin_village.site: A cliff-side village under a lighthouse on the Stormhaven coast, with steep stairs and nets hung from the cliff edge.
