koeglin_village.mystery: Nets draw up salt water from a stretch of bay where there is no sea beneath the nets. The village measures the water with a brass drip-cup.
clues: a brass drip-cup wired to the totem
nets that come up wet but empty
a lighthouse lamp trimmed to a slow pulse
koeglin_village.payoff: A brass drip-cup, an instrument to measure the giant's tears.
koeglin_village.rumour: The Koeglin nets are hauling up salt water from where there's no water to haul.

weeping_giant.name: Weeping Giant
weeping_giant.site: An inn built under a toppled stone giant, whose cheek is wet at every hour and whose tears fall into a basin by the door.
weeping_giant.mystery: The giant is a Direnni construct that drinks from a pump. Its tears are not tears but the overflow. The innkeeper has collected a brimming cup of it.
clues: a basin that never empties
a cheek-stone stained with salt
a hand-cranked drain-wheel in the cellar
weeping_giant.payoff: A cup of the giant's tears, which shows the pump's location.
weeping_giant.rumour: The giant over the Weeping Giant inn weeps salt. Folk say it is the sea trying to get out.
weeping_giant.thread_clue: a giant's cheek whose tears slow to a single drop a minute

evermor.name: Evermor
evermor.site: A city on lake islands linked by long stone causeways, with a central cathedral and boat-lanes that seem to float at dawn.
evermor.mystery: The lake level is rising. The causeways, built to a mark, have begun to flood; the city's engineers have traced the source to a drain beneath the water.
clues: a water-gauge with an old mark sunk below the surface
causeway stones waterlogged and cracked
a boat-lane that now has a current
evermor.payoff: The engineer's survey: a drain-line to Balfiera.

isle_of_balfiera.name: Isle of Balfiera
isle_of_balfiera.site: A hill-island with a ring of ruined towers in the bay, half-sunk at high tide.
isle_of_balfiera.mystery: The towers are a lock on the drain, and the island is sinking by a hand per year. It would rise if the pump stopped.
clues: a ring of towers with water-marks at four heights
a stone tide-gauge cut into the island's side
a causeway that appears at low tide only
isle_of_balfiera.payoff: A key-bar from the lock tower that fits the pump's mechanism.
isle_of_balfiera.rumour: The Isle of Balfiera is a few inches lower each year, though the tides are the same.

mthartzel.name: Mthartzel
mthartzel.site: A Dwemer cliff-bastion with a bridge-and-gear gate and high steam halls above a drained cavern.
mthartzel.mystery: The pump sits in the lowest hall, still drinking from the drowned cavern. Its keeper is a brass attendant who no longer remembers what it is pumping.
clues: a pump-arm rising and falling with no operator
a gauge needle pointing to 'tide'
a brass attendant polishing a valve
mthartzel.payoff: The pump's brake-lever, a unique tool that closes the drain.
mthartzel.rumour: Mthartzel's steam rises on the hour, and every hour a little more water vanishes from the bay.
mthartzel.thread_clue: a dial in a pump hall set to a gauge's wrong figure

direnni_tower.name: Direnni Tower
direnni_tower.site: A tall white elven tower on an island, the old Direnni seat, with a spiral stair and a crystal lens at the summit.
direnni_tower.mystery: The Direnni built the giant out of grief for a fallen queen. The tower's lens still points at the toppled statue. The last Direnni heir has never left.
clues: a lens aimed at the giant across the bay
a queen's portrait with the face worn smooth
stairs polished by a single occupant
direnni_tower.payoff: The lens-focus, a unique crystal that heals the land the giant drained.
direnni_tower.rumour: The old white tower of the Direnni stands on its island and a light burns in its lens-room every night. No one has been seen to climb the stair.

the_silver_pilgrim.name: The Silver Pilgrim
the_silver_pilgrim.site: A roadhouse on the Dragontail road, a long low building with a well-yard and a tally-board hung from the eaves.
the_silver_pilgrim.mystery: The tally-board lists every caravan's water-tithe in a dead man's handwriting. The keeper cannot account for who updates it.
clues: a tally-board updated overnight
a well-yard with every bucket tagged by a number
a roadhouse bell cast with a goat's head
the_silver_pilgrim.payoff: A well-token to present to the oasis keeper.
the_silver_pilgrim.rumour: The Silver Pilgrim's tally-board gets a new line every dawn, in a hand nobody knows.

goats_head_oasis.name: Goat's Head Oasis
goats_head_oasis.site: A well-oasis with palms and a half-buried statue of a goat, its horns visible above the sand.
goats_head_oasis.mystery: The statue's horns line up with a vanished shaft. The oasis water is falling each season, and there are older wells beneath the sand that were capped.
clues: a goat statue with horns aligned to the east
a capped older well under the sand
palms leaning toward the statue
goats_head_oasis.payoff: A well-cap key that lifts the oldest well-cap, and the shaft-map beneath it.
goats_head_oasis.rumour: The Goat's Head well is an inch lower every season, and the goat statue is half-buried now.

sentinel.name: Sentinel
sentinel.site: A harbour capital of domes with a vast palace dome, striped awnings and an oasis garden square.
sentinel.mystery: A water-merchant of the harbour has been buying caravan debts. His warehouse holds a roll of wells, each owed to the 'dune-king'.
clues: a water-merchant with an immense debt-roll
an oasis garden square with a dry fountain
harbour casks stamped with a goat's head
sentinel.payoff: The debt-roll: a complete list of the wells owed.

volenfell.name: Volenfell
volenfell.site: A Dwemer ruin under a dune, half-flooded with sand, with mechanical halls and drifts.
volenfell.mystery: The Dwemer here built the pumps that the dune-king used to tap the aquifer. One pump still turns under the sand, drawing the water down.
clues: a pump-wheel turning in a drift
sand drifting upward in the lowest hall
a plate stamped with a goat and a tally
volenfell.payoff: A pump-key that can stop the draw.
volenfell.rumour: Volenfell hums when the wind is right. The old shepherds say it drinks.
volenfell.thread_clue: a dial half in a sand-drift, its hand still ticking

motalion_necropolis.name: Motalion Necropolis
motalion_necropolis.site: A tiered necropolis cut into a cliff, crowded with sarcophagus niches and a lightless stair.
motalion_necropolis.mystery: The dune-king's heralds are buried here, and one niche is empty and warm. The inscriptions record every water-tithe ever collected.
clues: a niche that is empty and warm
an inscription of tithes in rows
a stair worn smooth by a barefoot herald
motalion_necropolis.payoff: A herald's seal that gets its bearer an audience.
motalion_necropolis.rumour: The necropolis at Motalion has a cold wind that blows out of the empty niche.

tuwhaccas_throne.name: Tuwhacca's Throne
tuwhaccas_throne.site: A ceremonial throne-hall of an ancient king with a procession of statues, colossal doors and a long colonnade.
tuwhaccas_throne.mystery: The throne faces a door sealed with sand. The king's last decree is carved on its arm: the city shall not be opened until the wells are paid in full.
clues: a throne with a decree carved on its arm
statues all turned to a sealed door
a colonnade whose last pillar is a standing man
tuwhaccas_throne.rumour: At Tuwhacca's Throne the statues' heads all face a door. Some mornings one has moved.
tuwhaccas_throne.thread_clue: a throne with an arm sawn clean away

lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.name: Lost City of the Na-Totambu
lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.site: A buried city under the dunes, sand-choked streets below ground, a sunken temple and glass-roofed houses lit by a thin shaft of light.
lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.mystery: The great cistern sits under the glass roof. Something sits in the dry basin and drinks in the shaft of light. It is both king and herald.
clues: a cistern basin with a single wet footprint
a glass roof with a shaft of light that moves
a king's chair with a bell on its arm
lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.payoff: The King's bell: a unique relic that calls water.
lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.rumour: At noon the lost city lets a single beam through its glass roof, and the dunes above seem to breathe.

valley_of_scars.name: Valley of Scars
valley_of_scars.site: A canyon whose walls are carved with battle-reliefs from rim to floor, in a rust-red stone.
valley_of_scars.mystery: A relief at the canyon mouth is carved fresh each season. It shows a staircase and a dozen travellers, and the faces change to match whoever visited last.
clues: a fresh relief with chisel dust still on the ledge
faces in the carving that look like recent visitors
a gap in the relief where one traveller stands unfinished
valley_of_scars.payoff: A rubbing of the unfinished panel.
valley_of_scars.rumour: A fresh scene appears on the Valley of Scars each season. Guides now sell tours before it fills in.

elinhir.name: Elinhir
elinhir.site: A mountain-city of tiers on a granite spur, with long stairs, windy ramparts and one blue-pennanted spire.
elinhir.mystery: The star-watchers compared the valley's reliefs with their charts. The last panel matches no sky they have recorded, but it matches one they will.
clues: a star-chart with a blank constellation
an observatory logbook with a prophecy crossed out
a spire with a sundial that runs ahead
elinhir.payoff: A star-chart of the coming sky.

dragonstar.name: Dragonstar
dragonstar.site: A fortress-city with a huge circular arena at its heart, spokes of streets running to a ringed wall and a stepped palace beyond.
dragonstar.mystery: The arena-master stages fights so that each bout matches a panel in the valley. Fighters who refuse wake bruised the next morning anyway.
clues: an arena floor carved with the relief's staircase
a master's schedule matched to panels
fighters' scars in the shape of carved figures
dragonstar.payoff: The arena-master's schedule: which panels have been fulfilled.
dragonstar.rumour: The arena-master of Dragonstar sets his bouts by a schedule he keeps in a locked chest, and the fighters who have read it won't discuss it.

aetherian_archive.name: Aetherian Archive
aetherian_archive.site: A giant sealed library sphere half out of the sand, its surface covered in turning glyph-rings.
aetherian_archive.mystery: The sphere's rings turn to the relief's staircase. Inside lies the only complete copy of the panels, in a language that predates the valley.
clues: glyph-rings aligned to a staircase
a seam in the sphere that opens at dusk
a library lectern with a relief rubbing under glass
aetherian_archive.payoff: The complete panel-roll, with the final panel's meaning.
aetherian_archive.rumour: The great sphere's rings turn at dusk, always to the same heading. Scholars come to watch and write nothing down.

sanctum_ophidia.name: Sanctum Ophidia
sanctum_ophidia.site: A serpent-cult sanctum of coiled-column rooms with spiral ramps, scale-patterned floors and a mirror-pool.
sanctum_ophidia.mystery: The serpent cult reads the last panel as the world-eater's coming. They coil their pool-mirror at the stair's top and ask to be swallowed when it comes.
clues: a mirror-pool showing the stair
coiled columns scored with a countdown
robes laid out for guests with serpent scales
sanctum_ophidia.payoff: A cult key that opens the pinnacle's stair-door.
sanctum_ophidia.rumour: The serpent cult of Sanctum Ophidia coils its pool-mirror toward the stair and awaits an end to the world with perfect good manners.

skyreach_pinnacle.name: Skyreach Pinnacle
skyreach_pinnacle.site: A spire of rock standing alone in dunes, ringed by stairs that wind to a small platform at the top.
skyreach_pinnacle.mystery: The platform is where the last panel shows a figure stepping off. The cult wants the figure to fall. The arena-master wants it to jump.
clues: a platform with a worn step-off notch
stairs with names scratched on the risers
wind that sings a single note at dusk
skyreach_pinnacle.payoff: A unique panel-chip that can rewrite a carved fate.
skyreach_pinnacle.rumour: The lone spire of Skyreach has a stair wound around it and a step-off notch at the top. The cult wants a figure to fall, and so does the arena.

thrall_cove.name: Thrall Cove
thrall_cove.site: A slavers' former cove with rotting pens on a half-tide beach and a cliff stair of rusted rings.
thrall_cove.mystery: The cove has been bought, in a single sale, by a Hubalajad steward. He pays freedmen to tend a garden he never shows them.
clues: rusted shackles hung on a post like wind-chimes
a freedmen's graveyard with new plantings
a deed-board stamped with a lord's palm-seal
thrall_cove.payoff: A freedman's contract with a palm-sealed clause.
thrall_cove.rumour: Thrall Cove's freedmen all have a palm-leaf pinned to their coat. They don't say what they plant.

abahs_landing.name: Abah's Landing
abahs_landing.site: A pier-and-stilt harbour on a bay, with rope walkways, nets and a lighthouse on a mole.
abahs_landing.mystery: Palm-seeds pass through the harbour in small sealed jars labelled 'for the garden'. The harbour-master has stopped asking whose garden.
clues: jars of palm seed on the dock
a customs form with the same palm-seal
a net of sleeping fishermen's palm-leaf charms
abahs_landing.payoff: A seed-jar manifest naming the lord's agents.
abahs_landing.rumour: The stilt harbour at Abah's Landing ships palm-seeds in sealed jars. Nobody knows which garden they are for, and the harbour-master has stopped asking.

taneth.name: Taneth
taneth.site: A seaside city on stepped cliff terraces, with a white palace over turquoise pools and long stair-lanes to a harbour.
taneth.mystery: The city's court physician has been asked to certify the death of freedmen who are not dead, so their debts may be sold on.
clues: a physician's stack of unsigned certificates
a court bench left empty at a freedman's trial
turquoise pools that smell of palms
taneth.payoff: A physician's confession with the lord's name.

hubalajad_palace.name: Hubalajad Palace
hubalajad_palace.site: A walled lord's estate in the Hews Bane hills, with a long colonnade and a conservatory of potted palms.
hubalajad_palace.mystery: The lord is long dead. His steward has kept his name and his appetite for gardens. The conservatory's palms are labelled with ancestors' names.
clues: potted palms tagged with ancestors' names
a steward's ledger of freedmen planted
a lord's chair under a dust sheet
hubalajad_palace.payoff: The steward's ledger: which freedmen are in the garden.
hubalajad_palace.rumour: At Hubalajad the lord has been dead twenty years and still orders palms by the barrow-load.

rihad.name: Rihad
rihad.site: A walled bazaar-city of narrow lanes under rope-and-cloth awnings with a single tall minaret and a scented spice gate.
rihad.mystery: A spice merchant sells a tincture made from the palm-bloom to buyers who ask no questions. The tincture is why the garden is guarded.
clues: a spice stall with an unlabelled tincture
a minaret clerk's desk with sealed orders
a courier with a palm-leaf pass
rihad.payoff: A tincture-phial that proves the garden's bloom heals.

ahaleb_necropolis.name: Ahaleb Necropolis
ahaleb_necropolis.site: A mid-size necropolis with a long bridge hall over a pit, a hidden oasis chamber of palms under skylights and a final stair of golden doors.
ahaleb_necropolis.mystery: The hidden chamber is the garden. Palms grow from the embalmed, and the freedmen tend them in a trance of wages and water. The gardener is the steward's master.
clues: palms rooted in sarcophagi
freedmen asleep on benches with a watering-can in hand
skylights ground to focus light on a single bloom
ahaleb_necropolis.payoff: A seed of the bloom that cures sand-fever and the gardener's ledger of names.
ahaleb_necropolis.rumour: Ahaleb has a garden underneath that glows green at noon, if you stand on the right dune.

port_hunding.name: Port Hunding
port_hunding.site: A small port gate and pier on Stros M'Kai's coast, a customs hut and a harbour crane, with a sealed manifest cabinet.
port_hunding.mystery: A manifest for the fifth-year ship is hidden behind a crate. Cargo: sealed. Return: not expected. The harbour clerk will not discuss it.
clues: a lever behind a harbour crate
a manifest line in red ink
a pier-plank branded with a prow
port_hunding.rumour: Every fifth year a ship leaves Port Hunding with sealed cargo and the clerks are told to stay home.
port_hunding.thread_clue: a harbour cabinet containing a page marked with a tide-glyph

saintsport.name: Saintsport
saintsport.site: A shrine harbour on the Stros M'Kai coast, with a shrine to a drowned saint and a bell that rings under water.
saintsport.mystery: The saint is a captain of the first fifth-year ship, who volunteered to be lost. The shrine's bell rings when a descendant is chosen.
clues: a shrine bell that rings under water
family names painted on the harbour wall
wreaths on the water at every fifth spring
saintsport.payoff: A shrine-token to be presented at the inn.
saintsport.rumour: Saintsport's bell rings under water every fifth year, and a family goes quiet.

draggin_tale_inn.name: Draggin Tale Inn
draggin_tale_inn.site: An inn with a giant draconian tail over the door, a long common room and a back room where the families meet.
draggin_tale_inn.mystery: The tail is a ship's prow-figure, not a dragon's. The families sit at the long table every fifth year to choose the next captain by lot.
clues: a long table with twelve seats
a prow-figure's scales rusted green
a lottery bowl of small carved prows
draggin_tale_inn.payoff: A carved prow, the captain's lot, which grants passage on the fifth-year ship.
draggin_tale_inn.rumour: The Draggin Tale's back room is shut every fifth spring while twelve families draw lots.

stros_mkai.name: Stros M'Kai
stros_mkai.site: A rocky island town with a lighthouse and fort at the harbour mouth and tight alleys climbing the central hill.
stros_mkai.mystery: The harbour treaty that freed the island carried a clause: a ship must sail beyond the horizon every fifth year or the treaty lapses. The lighthouse's lower floor holds the clause.
clues: a treaty plate in the lighthouse base
a harbour-mouth beacon that points at the horizon
a fort drill that salutes a ship that is not there
stros_mkai.thread_clue: a lighthouse plate with a tide-glyph hidden in its border

onsis_breath.name: Onsi's Breath
onsis_breath.site: A ring of wind-carved arches on the Bangkorai coast, whose stones sing in the wind with a hollow note.
onsis_breath.mystery: The arches are fused vertebrae of a vast sea-beast. The torn page of the Tide-Ledger lies in a niche in the largest arch.
clues: arches humming a hollow note
a niche in the largest arch with a flat stone cover
a whale-bone inscription of tides
onsis_breath.payoff: The torn Tide-Ledger page with tide-hours.
onsis_breath.rumour: Onsi's arches hum on a westerly. The sailors say the wind is reading tides aloud.
onsis_breath.thread_clue: a singing arch with one vertebra replaced by a plain stone

star_haven_adeptorium.name: Star Haven Adeptorium
star_haven_adeptorium.site: A tiny academy under a dome on an Anequina hillside, with a roof opening and brass quadrants on every windowsill.
star_haven_adeptorium.mystery: The academy's mage has measured Secunda rising late for eleven months. The priests call it error and refuse to share their almanac.
clues: quadrants on every windowsill, all aimed at one gap
an observation log with a column of minutes
a roof dome with scorch marks from priests' lamps
star_haven_adeptorium.payoff: The mage's observation log and a lunar chart.
star_haven_adeptorium.rumour: The Star Haven mage says Secunda is late and gets laughed at. He keeps measuring anyway.

shrine_of_the_cats_divine.name: Shrine of the Cats Divine
shrine_of_the_cats_divine.site: A stepped shrine of giant cat statues on an Anequina hillside, with a moon-pool and a stair of prayer tablets.
shrine_of_the_cats_divine.mystery: The statues' shadows no longer line up with the shrine's moon-mark at moonrise. Someone has chipped a new mark into the pool's lip, hastily, to hide the drift.
clues: a new moon-mark chipped into the pool's lip
shadows misaligned by a hand's width
prayer tablets with the dates scraped and re-cut
shrine_of_the_cats_divine.payoff: A rubbing of the old moon-mark.
shrine_of_the_cats_divine.rumour: The great cats at the shrine have started casting shadows that don't match the day.

torval.name: Torval
torval.site: A capital of concentric rings with a palace of two linked domes at the centre and a processional road aligned to moonrise.
torval.mystery: The Moon-Priests keep two almanacs: a true one in the palace dome and a public one. The true almanac shows the drift. Only the high priest may read it.
clues: a palace dome with a locked inner almanac chamber
a procession road re-paved to a new alignment
priests' lamps lit at the old moonrise
torval.payoff: A copy of the true almanac.

temple_of_agamanus.name: Temple of Agamanus
temple_of_agamanus.site: A ridge-top temple with terraces in four stages, prayer-wheels and a hollow dome, whose sanctum is aligned to a single moonrise.
temple_of_agamanus.mystery: The alignment is wrong now. The sanctum's lamp lights seven minutes after the moon touches the dome, and the temple keepers have stopped lighting the lamp.
clues: a sanctum lamp left unlit
prayer-wheels stilled by wedges
a dome with a brass line scored over by a second line
temple_of_agamanus.payoff: A key-wheel which sets the choir-tomb's tuning.
temple_of_agamanus.rumour: The temple of Agamanus no longer lights its lamp. The keepers say it will be lit again once the moon is on time.

tomb_of_the_moon_singers.name: Tomb of the Moon Singers
tomb_of_the_moon_singers.site: A choir-tomb of echoing chambers, each room tuned to a note of the moon's phase, cut into an Anequina hill.
tomb_of_the_moon_singers.mystery: Every chamber has drifted out of tune, a half-tone flat. The singers' choir-mistress stands at the lowest room and sings the true note, once a night.
clues: tuning-forks stacked in wall niches
a chamber whose echo returns a half-tone flat
a choir-mistress's footprints in dust, going down
tomb_of_the_moon_singers.payoff: A tuning-fork which fits the vault's keyed moon-gates.
tomb_of_the_moon_singers.rumour: The Moon Singers' tomb hums a note lower than it did when my mother was a kitten.

vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.name: Vault of the Heavenly Scourge
vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.site: A sealed vault of lunar weapons, a long hall of racked blades that wake when moonlight enters the skylights and an antechamber of three keyed moon-gates.
vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.mystery: The blades wake seven minutes late, and in the interval they hunger. The gates' three keys no longer fit by moonlight alone: each needs a note to turn.
clues: racked blades that tremble in the dark
skylights stained with seven minutes of dawn-light
three keyholes shaped like crescents with a notch missing
vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.payoff: A unique lunar blade, the moonblade of the mane, and the real almanac.
vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.rumour: The vault's blades hum at moonrise. Folk say they have started to hum before the moon comes.

roadside_twin_moons.name: Roadside Twin Moons
roadside_twin_moons.site: A roadhouse with two lanterns by the Rimmen road, one pale and one rose, each the colour of a moon.
roadside_twin_moons.mystery: The lanterns' keeper found a burial mask in a traveller's pack and hid it in the second lantern's urn. A faceless Khajiit bowed to him last night.
clues: an urn behind the second lantern
a faceless traveller's footprints
a mask with its mouth stuffed with a receipt
roadside_twin_moons.payoff: A burial mask and a receipt naming a caravan stop.
roadside_twin_moons.rumour: A faceless Khajiit walked past the Twin Moons last night and bowed to the lanterns.

baandari_caravan_stop.name: Baandari Caravan Stop
baandari_caravan_stop.site: A tent camp by the Rimmen road with painted wagons, cooking fires and a bright awning for the trade.
baandari_caravan_stop.mystery: The Baandari buy masks cheap from grave-robbers and sell them to collectors abroad. The caravan-mother doesn't know the masks have been the dead's faces.
clues: a tent of wrapped masks in hay
a caravan-mother's account book with 'faces' as a column
a wagon painted with a face that is not a face
baandari_caravan_stop.payoff: The caravan-mother's account of who sells her the masks.
baandari_caravan_stop.rumour: The Baandari tent camp by the Rimmen road will sell you anything, and lately that includes carved faces nobody asks about.
baandari_caravan_stop.thread_clue: a tent of caravan-slips all stamped with the same watermark

hakoshae.name: Hakoshae
hakoshae.site: A hamlet around a ring of upright moonstones where tomb-guardians live, low houses in the circle's shadow.
hakoshae.mystery: The guardians have run out of graves for the faceless who come asking for faces. They keep them in the circle at night, bound by moonlight, and weep.
clues: faceless figures standing within the circle at night
low houses with a mask hung over each door
a ring stone chipped at the base where a name was
hakoshae.payoff: A circle-stone key which lets a bearer into the necropolis' upper tier.
hakoshae.rumour: The Hakoshae guardians keep faceless dead in the ring at night. Don't walk near after dark.

rimmen.name: Rimmen
rimmen.site: A cliff city of artisans with a palace on the high cliff, craft districts stepped below and a necropolis door cut at its base.
rimmen.mystery: The city's mask-carvers are paid to make blanks for the dead, but the commissions have tripled and none of the buyers are Rimmen's. The carvers' guild has stopped counting.
clues: a mask-carvers' shop with a queue of foreign buyers
a necropolis door with a chain freshly oiled
a guild ledger with sums that no longer add up
rimmen.payoff: The carvers' ledger, with the buyers' names.

anequina_aqueduct.name: Anequina Aqueduct
anequina_aqueduct.site: A long arched aqueduct across a gorge, with a channel on top and maintenance galleries running through its piers.
anequina_aqueduct.mystery: The aqueduct's galleries are a smuggler's route. The masks pass under the water in lead boxes, so the necropolis guards never see them leave.
clues: lead boxes in an arch recess
a channel-gate with a secret second latch
a gallery lamp lit only on moonless nights
anequina_aqueduct.payoff: A gallery key, opening the smugglers' door under the necropolis.
anequina_aqueduct.rumour: The aqueduct's piers are hollow, and on moonless nights lamps burn inside them.
anequina_aqueduct.thread_clue: an aqueduct channel that falls silent, its stones humming a lullaby

rimmen_necropolis.name: Rimmen Necropolis
rimmen_necropolis.site: A vast city of the dead in layers, with crypt avenues, moon-lit atria and a lunar clock chamber that descends with the moons' cycle.
rimmen_necropolis.mystery: In the lunar clock chamber stand the empty mask-niches. Each must be filled before the moon is full, or the faceless will not rest.
clues: an empty niche on every column of the clock chamber
a lunar clock stopped between two phases
a path of footprints that all end in a single niche
rimmen_necropolis.payoff: The honoured dead's masks restored: a unique mask that lets the wearer walk among the dead.
rimmen_necropolis.rumour: The Rimmen necropolis has a clock that stopped between two moons. Some say it is waiting for faces.

tathara_sugar_farm.name: Tathara Sugar Farm
tathara_sugar_farm.site: A sugar farm with a boil-house at the edge of a meadow where the cane is lit with a faint, moon-coloured glow.
tathara_sugar_farm.mystery: This season's moon-sugar glows too bright and tastes of iron. The farmer's wife slept three days after a spoonful.
clues: a sugar-jar that hums when set down
cane rows bright enough to read by
a boil-house chimney that smokes violet
tathara_sugar_farm.payoff: A humming jar: evidence the glow is not natural.
tathara_sugar_farm.rumour: The Tathara sugar is brighter than any harvest. It tastes of iron, and the wife sleeps three days.
tathara_sugar_farm.thread_clue: a farm ledger with three pages stamped by an unfamiliar seal

moon_sugar_meadow.name: Moon-Sugar Meadow
moon_sugar_meadow.site: A field of luminous moon-sugar flowers in a shallow bowl of pale earth, brightest along a drainage ditch.
moon_sugar_meadow.mystery: The ditch drains from a sealed hall of the Dwemer. The meadow's glow is a coolant, and the flowers drink it.
clues: a ditch glowing brighter than the flowers
a flagstone in the ditch stamped with a gear
flowers bent toward a single drain grate
moon_sugar_meadow.payoff: A drain-grate key to the colossus hall.
moon_sugar_meadow.rumour: The meadow glows brightest along the ditch, and the ditch never freezes.
moon_sugar_meadow.thread_clue: an urn holding a debt-slip with a crescent-and-ledger watermark

the_prancing_netch.name: The Prancing Netch
the_prancing_netch.site: An inn built beneath a hanging netch-balloon on the Anequina road, with a long common room and a rooftop landing for ropes.
the_prancing_netch.mystery: The inn's cellar is the Dwemer drain's overflow tank. The innkeeper has tasted the glowing oil and says it makes the beer interesting.
clues: a cellar tank glowing blue-green
a beer-tap handle cast of brass with a gear on it
a balloon rope that ties to a pipe-end
the_prancing_netch.rumour: The Prancing Netch's beer glows faintly on Fridays and nobody will say why.

corinthe.name: Corinthe
corinthe.site: A green river city of terraced gardens, canals with arching bridges and a garden-roofed cathedral.
corinthe.mystery: The cathedral's herbalists have identified the sleep-sickness as a symptom of the glow. They have a cure grown from a river-moss and no way to afford more.
clues: a cathedral herbarium with a glowing bed
hospital cots of sleepwalkers in the nave
a ledger of costs with a red 'unpaid' stamp
corinthe.payoff: A herbalist's cure-moss, which cleanses the glow.
corinthe.rumour: The cathedral of Corinthe has a ward of sleepers laid out like a field of sheaves, and the herbalists say the cure costs more than the town has.

senchal.name: Senchal
senchal.site: A port of terraced sugar warehouses with stepped white roofs, striped awnings and sugar-boil chimneys.
senchal.mystery: The boil-houses cut the refined sugar with colossus dust, because the dust makes it glow brighter and sell faster. The boil-masters know the cost.
clues: boil-house sacks stamped with a gear
a warehouse where the dust is mixed at night
a quay-side sugar-barrel that glows through the slats
senchal.payoff: A boil-master's confession and a sack of colossus dust.
senchal.thread_clue: a warehouse wall with a ledger-and-moon plate screwed to it

halls_of_colossus.name: Halls of Colossus
halls_of_colossus.site: A Dwemer hall of colossal machines with too-large doors and a giant half-assembled construct whose chest is cracked.
halls_of_colossus.mystery: The colossus's cracked chest weeps coolant down the ditch. If it is sealed, the meadow's glow will fade and the sugar will be only sweet.
clues: a colossus's chest weeping a luminous oil
doors three times human height
a gantry of brass lines leading to a drain
halls_of_colossus.payoff: A colossus seal-plate, a unique that closes the leak.
halls_of_colossus.rumour: The Halls of Colossus drip at night. The sugar-folk say the meadow grows from its tears.
halls_of_colossus.thread_clue: a dial in the colossus's chest that has turned nearly full circle

orcrest.name: Orcrest
orcrest.site: A mesa-top fort-town in orange rock, with a gate shaped like a pair of claws, cisterns and rooftop banners.
orcrest.mystery: Every caravan out of Orcrest carries one blade-shard with a ribbon. The guard-captain says it is an old custom. He does not know what the shards are for.
clues: a gatepost scored with a hundred crosses
caravan wagons each with one shard tied to the axle
banners with a single sword stitched half-broken
orcrest.payoff: A blade-shard tied with a red ribbon.
orcrest.rumour: Every caravan out of Orcrest carries one broken blade-shard. Nobody knows who sends them.

dune.name: Dune
dune.site: A caravan crossroads with a wheel-shaped market, eight radial lanes, striped tents and camel pens at the rim.
dune.mystery: All eight lanes of the market end at the same wagon, which sells nothing. It stores the shards until a caravan-mother has enough for a full carry.
clues: a wagon at the wheel's hub that sells nothing
eight lanes marked with different blades
a camel whose saddle is a sheath of shards
dune.payoff: A caravan-mother's ledger of the blade-shards' carry.
dune.rumour: The caravan market at Dune has a wagon at its hub that sells nothing and is never left unguarded.

ne_quin_al.name: Ne Quin-al
ne_quin_al.site: An ancient ruined city on a plateau, with a processional road, collapsed towers and a single standing arch.
ne_quin_al.mystery: The old city's smiths were the first to swear on blades. Their oath-hall is the last stop before the hill. A tally of oaths decorates its floor.
clues: a floor tally of oaths in nine hundred columns
a standing arch with a sword-shaped keystone
a forge-hall with a cold anvil that is warm to the touch
ne_quin_al.payoff: The oath-hall's broken sword: the first piece of the great blade.
ne_quin_al.rumour: At Ne Quin-al the old smiths' oath-hall has a floor that someone has been tallying by hand, and the smith's anvil is warm to the touch.

hill_of_shattered_swords.name: Hill of Shattered Swords
hill_of_shattered_swords.site: A hill planted with thousands of broken sword-blades, shining in the wind like a cold field of wheat.
hill_of_shattered_swords.mystery: Each season the shards on the hill rearrange themselves into a ring around a hollow where a single whole blade should stand. It is still not whole.
clues: shards arranged in a ring around a hollow
a shard at the centre with a ribbon from every caravan
wind that rings the shards in a single chord
hill_of_shattered_swords.payoff: A hundred-oath shard that fits the quenching trough.
hill_of_shattered_swords.rumour: The shards on the hill move at night. By morning they are in a ring, and there is always a gap.

prowls_edge_dragonscour.name: Prowl's Edge Dragonscour
prowls_edge_dragonscour.site: A ridge of colossal bones leading to a lair on a mesa, an open-air scour you can walk inside with ribs forming arches.
prowls_edge_dragonscour.mystery: The dragon's ribcage is the quench-trough where the great blade is made. The blade that rises is a hundred oaths heavy, and the lair's guardian wants it back in the bone.
clues: a rib-arch scored with tally marks
a bone trough full of cold water that steams
a blade-shaped hollow in the sand under the ribs
prowls_edge_dragonscour.payoff: The oath-forged blade, a unique relic that binds its wielder's word.
prowls_edge_dragonscour.rumour: At Prowl's Edge a steam rises from the bones on a cold night, as if something were quenched.
prowls_edge_dragonscour.thread_clue: a rib-arch with a clean saw-cut gap and a numbered tag

elden_tree.name: Elden Tree
elden_tree.site: The great tree seen from the whole province, a trunk wide as a hill with a faintly glowing crown above the clouds.
elden_tree.mystery: The crown's glow is dimming a shade each season. A root-totem at its base is studded with glass splinters, each fed a name by the keepers.
clues: a root-totem drilled with glowing splinters
a trunk-stair worn at the keepers' door
crown-leaves falling pale at the base
elden_tree.payoff: A glass splinter that opens the underground tower's door.
elden_tree.rumour: The great tree's glow is a shade dimmer than last year. The keepers say it will be fine. The keepers are not looking up.

ne_salas.name: Ne Salas
ne_salas.site: A tower-city underground, a spiral of ring galleries around a central crystal pillar, bright and cold.
ne_salas.mystery: The central pillar is the tree-lamp's twin, the star-lamp's counterpart. Each gallery holds a ring of names the Ayleid wrote to feed it.
clues: ring galleries lined with name-plates
a crystal pillar bright at its heart
a lift-platform that rises toward the roots
ne_salas.payoff: A ring of Ayleid names, enough to feed the crown for a season.
ne_salas.rumour: Under the great tree is a second light, say the root-diggers, one that doesn't flicker.
ne_salas.thread_clue: a central pillar warm to the hand with an unfamiliar white

reliquary_of_stars.name: Reliquary of Stars
reliquary_of_stars.site: A domed observatory-vault whose ceiling is a map of the night sky in inlaid crystal, with floor rings that rotate by lever.
reliquary_of_stars.mystery: Each lit star in the ceiling opens an archive niche of names. Half the stars have gone dark, because the Ayleid keepers' successors no longer renew them.
clues: a ceiling with half its stars dark
floor rings turned to a stale alignment
an archive niche packed with unspoken name-scrolls
reliquary_of_stars.payoff: A star-lit scroll of renewal names that can be fed to the crown.
reliquary_of_stars.rumour: Under the reliquary's dome the stars go out one by one. The cartographers swear it was full of them a decade ago.
reliquary_of_stars.thread_clue: ceiling stars re-lit in a pattern that points southwest

elden_root.name: Elden Root
elden_root.site: A city built into and around one colossal tree, with root markets, spiral stairs inside the trunk and three canopy tiers of platforms.
elden_root.mystery: The Green Pact's keepers meet in a locked hall at the crown. They have debated for a generation whether to feed the lamp with Bosmer names. Nobody wants to be first.
clues: a locked keepers' hall at the crown
a ballot-urn with a single name inside
a trunk-stair carved with a crown and a ring of blank glyphs
elden_root.payoff: The keepers' ballot, and the key to the ossuary's lowest tier.

ossuary_of_telacar.name: Ossuary of Telacar
ossuary_of_telacar.site: A bone-walled ossuary built in terraced galleries, skulls arranged by family line, each tier's door answering to a name read aloud.
ossuary_of_telacar.mystery: The lowest tier is flooded. The name that would open it was the last Ayleid lamp-warden's, long forgotten. When read, it calls the crown to full light.
clues: skull rows labelled by lineage
a door that answers only to a read-aloud name
a flooded lowest tier with a lamp floating on the water
ossuary_of_telacar.payoff: The lamp-warden's name and the crown's full light: a unique relic that lights without fuel.
ossuary_of_telacar.rumour: The Ossuary doors will open if you read the right name aloud. Nobody remembers the right name.

roadside_green_bough.name: Roadside Green Bough
roadside_green_bough.site: An inn in a boughed tree on the Malabal Tor road, with stair-ladders and a landing of woven rope.
roadside_green_bough.mystery: The innkeeper's route-board shows the walking city's path in two lines: the old seasonal route and a straight charcoal line toward a hollow tree.
clues: a route-board with a second charcoal line
a pair of tree-cutters' axes left at the stair
a cut stump with fresh sap
roadside_green_bough.payoff: The route-board's charcoal line and a hermit's address.
roadside_green_bough.rumour: The walking city has been going in a straight line since spring. The innkeeper drew it on the wall.

supplication_house.name: Supplication House
supplication_house.site: A hermit's hut deep in Malabal Tor with a prayer-bench, a wind-chime of bone and a ring of stumps around it.
supplication_house.mystery: The hermit has been cutting guide-trees to break the apostates' chant. She counts each stump as a sin and a service.
clues: a ring of fresh stumps with prayer-ribbons
a wind-chime of bone that rings off-pitch
a chant tablet with a Pact-curse scratched through
supplication_house.payoff: A tablet of the apostates' chant, and a map of the guide-trees.
supplication_house.rumour: The hermit at Supplication House is cutting trees and weeping while she does it. The wardens pretend not to hear.

drabul.name: Drabul
drabul.site: An Orc outpost in the Malabal forest, a palisade of cut trunks and a forge-pit beneath a canopy hole.
drabul.mystery: The Orcs of Drabul were hired by the hermit to fell guide-trees. They do not hold to the Pact but have been warned; their axes are marked with strange glyphs.
clues: axes marked with a guide-tree glyph
a log pile of cut guide-trunks
a chief's tally of stumps felled
drabul.payoff: The chief's tally of felled guide-trees.
drabul.rumour: The Orcs of Drabul have been felling trees that Bosmer would not touch, and no Bosmer has said a word against them.

jathsogur.name: Jathsogur
jathsogur.site: An Orc stronghold on a ridge above the forest, with a stone keep and a view of the guide-tree line.
jathsogur.mystery: From the ridge, the straight line of the walking city's route is clear. The stronghold has been shooting down the last guide-trees with ballistae.
clues: a ballista aimed at a lone tall tree
a map-table with the guide-line inked
arrows fletched with a Pact-curse mark
jathsogur.payoff: The last guide-tree's bearing and a ballista bolt.
jathsogur.rumour: From Jathsogur's wall you can see the city's route. The Orcs have been shooting at the trees along it.

silvenar.name: Silvenar
silvenar.site: A hidden court under hollowed root arches, a sheltered amphitheatre of roots with a single audience hall lit by fireflies.
silvenar.mystery: The court knows of the apostates' chant and has done nothing, for the chant is the dissolution of the Pact itself. A court councillor passes the cutters coin in secret.
clues: a root arch carved with the walking city's route
a council chair left empty
fireflies that gather on a map
silvenar.payoff: A court seal, giving access to the walking city's inner stairs.
silvenar.rumour: The hidden court at Silvenar knows who is cutting guide-trees, and a councillor passes the cutters coin in secret.

falinesti.name: Falinesti
falinesti.site: A tree-city that is in a different place each season, with four sites of the same tree-plan in different foliage.
falinesti.mystery: The city is leaning in its walk toward the hollow tree. Its lowest roots have found the line; in a month its trunk will be wedged in the tomb mouth.
clues: roots running in a single straight furrow
a harbour of rope-bridges that bows toward the east
a council that has stopped meeting
falinesti.payoff: A root-cutter's chisel, to sever the walker's final guiding root.

tomb_of_the_apostates.name: Tomb of the Apostates
tomb_of_the_apostates.site: A hollow great tree whose heartwood is carved with tombs, stairs spiralling inside the trunk.
tomb_of_the_apostates.mystery: The apostates' chant rises from the lowest tier, every dusk. They believe the walker will bring them communion; it will bring a tonne of root.
clues: a chanting figure at the base of the hollow
stairs worn only on one side
heartwood carved with a walking tree
tomb_of_the_apostates.payoff: The chant-stone: a unique that silences or turns a tree-walker.
tomb_of_the_apostates.rumour: At dusk the hollow tree sings. The Pact-wardens put their hands over their ears and call it wind.
tomb_of_the_apostates.thread_clue: a heartwood panel prised out, the cut still weeping sap

marbruk.name: Marbruk
marbruk.site: A fort-town in a glade ringed by a living wall of thorn and stone, with a central fire pit and watch posts.
marbruk.mystery: The thorn-wall's plaque lists forty Ayleid names pricked in thorns. Never cut, never move. The wall's keepers add to it each solstice.
clues: a thorn plaque with forty pricked names
a fire-pit with a ring of undried stones
watchers who bow to the wall at dusk
marbruk.payoff: A thorn that opens the orchard's inner ring.
marbruk.rumour: The thorn wall of Marbruk has names pricked into it. The watchers bow every dusk and nobody asks why.

woodhearth.name: Woodhearth
woodhearth.site: A harbour city of Greenshade grown from a ring of living trees, with rope-and-plank bridges strung among their boughs.
woodhearth.mystery: The ring of trees leans by a finger a year to the south. The city's gardeners wedge it with stakes; the trees patiently push them out.
clues: wedge-stakes bent and snapped
a ring of trees all tilted the same way
bark carved with faces that look south
woodhearth.payoff: A leaf of the orchard that retains an Ayleid voice.

labyrinth.name: Labyrinth
labyrinth.site: A hedge-and-root maze that rearranges each time you leave a junction, with carved arrows that lie and wisp-lights as false guides.
labyrinth.mystery: The maze is the street-plan of the burned city, grown over: each junction was a crossing and each dead end a house. The exit is a gate.
clues: carved arrows pointing at walls
wisp-lights circling a junction
a ridge from which the maze looks like a map
labyrinth.payoff: The maze's true plan: a map to the burned city's gate.
labyrinth.rumour: The Labyrinth hedge changes each time you look away. From the ridge you can see it is a map.

city_of_ash.name: City of Ash
city_of_ash.site: A burned Ayleid city with ash-choked terraces, melted crystal lamps and a scorched grand cistern.
city_of_ash.mystery: The Ayleid lords burned their own lamps to keep their slaves from using them. The ash on the terraces is shaped like people. A single lamp still burns in the cistern.
clues: ash lying in the shapes of people
melted lamps in rows on the terraces
a single lamp lit in the dry cistern
city_of_ash.payoff: The cistern lamp: a unique crystal that lets the dead go home.
city_of_ash.rumour: The City of Ash is quiet. The ash holds the shape of people who sat down and did not get up.
city_of_ash.thread_clue: a cistern lamp relit in a field of ash

waterdancer_falls.name: Waterdancer Falls
waterdancer_falls.site: A tall waterfall in Reaper's March with a spray rainbow and a prayer-stone at its base cut with eight notches.
waterdancer_falls.mystery: Seven of the Truce's eight notches are filled with white bone. The eighth has been filled with red clay, a stand-in for a missing bone.
clues: a prayer-stone with seven white notches and one red
a spray rainbow that ends at the stone
offering-ribbons in two colours knotted together
waterdancer_falls.payoff: A clay thumb-print, an impression that can be matched to a hand.
waterdancer_falls.rumour: The prayer-stone at Waterdancer has eight notches and only seven bones. Both peoples avoid talking about the eighth.
waterdancer_falls.thread_clue: a waterfall whose spray rainbow flickers on the hour

sren_ja.name: Sren Ja
sren_ja.site: A tree village of Khajiit in Reaper's March, with rope-bridges between boughs and drums at every platform.
sren_ja.mystery: The village's drum-song carries the Truce's rite. The drummer who knew the eighth verse died without teaching it. The drums stop at the eighth beat.
clues: drums that stop at the eighth beat
a drummer's empty seat at the central platform
a bone-whistle carved with a gap
sren_ja.payoff: The first seven verses of the Truce-song.
sren_ja.rumour: At Sren Ja the drums stop at the eighth beat. The elders say it is for the dead drummer.

dokrin_monastery.name: Dokrin Monastery
dokrin_monastery.site: A forest monastery of the Khajiit with a courtyard of prayer-wheels and a small library of drum-scores.
dokrin_monastery.mystery: The monks hold the oldest drum-score of the Truce. The eighth verse has been cut out and replaced with a pressed leaf. The abbot weeps when asked.
clues: a drum-score with a pressed leaf where a verse was
prayer-wheels with their last panel blank
an abbot's cell with a clay thumb-mould on the shelf
dokrin_monastery.payoff: The pressed leaf, tracing a Bosmer hand.
dokrin_monastery.rumour: The monks at Dokrin keep the oldest drum-scores in the March. One page has been replaced with a pressed leaf, and the abbot weeps when anyone asks.

rawlkha.name: Rawlkha
rawlkha.site: A Khajiiti trade-town of canvas and bamboo stalls strung between trees, a lantern forest.
rawlkha.mystery: The Bosmer who cut the verse out sold it in the Rawlkha market, and the verse has changed hands eleven times. Each buyer wrote a gloss in the margin.
clues: a stall of manuscripts, one with a stolen verse
lantern strings in two colours
a margin gloss in a Bosmer hand
rawlkha.payoff: The stolen verse with eleven glosses.
rawlkha.rumour: Rawlkha's lantern-market sells paper from a dozen stalls, and a verse that was stolen from a monastery has passed through eleven hands there.
rawlkha.thread_clue: a lantern-market stall that sells only paper

arenthia.name: Arenthia
arenthia.site: A river-cliff town of gardens hung on rope terraces over a waterfall, with houses cut into the cliff face.
arenthia.mystery: A Bosmer scholar bought the verse to prove the Truce's rite was Bosmer in origin. She would rather the rite be forgotten than shared.
clues: a scholar's study with a pressed leaf in a frame
gardens divided by a thin line of two colours
a river gate where Bosmer and Khajiit boats avoid each other
arenthia.payoff: The scholar's confession and the verse restored.

thizzrini_arena.name: Thizzrini Arena
thizzrini_arena.site: A ruined arena in the jungle with a sand floor and tiers of stone seats half-eaten by roots.
thizzrini_arena.mystery: The arena was where the Truce's rite was danced. The sand holds the eighth step: a footprint of one dancer, neither Bosmer nor Khajiit.
clues: a sand floor with a single deep footprint
seats worn by two peoples' sitting
a dancers' gate with two doors facing each other
thizzrini_arena.payoff: The eighth step: a dance-form that fits the final verse.
thizzrini_arena.rumour: In the old arena a single footprint stays in the sand. No rain washes it out.

reapers_henge.name: Reaper's Henge
reapers_henge.site: A stone circle with a bone-white altar on a rise in Reaper's March, ringed by eight standing stones.
reapers_henge.mystery: The altar is a place for peace-bones. The eighth must be given by one who is both peoples and neither. The land asks the wanderer what they are.
clues: seven bones on the altar in a white ring
a vacant eighth bone-seat in red clay
stones with ribbons of both peoples' colours
reapers_henge.payoff: The eighth bone and the Truce renewed: a unique axe of the Wild Hunt.
reapers_henge.rumour: At the henge the altar is bright with bone. One seat has been empty for ten years.

isle_of_contemplation.name: Isle of Contemplation
isle_of_contemplation.site: A tiny isle off Auridon with a single meditation platform, a sundial and a boat-landing of white stone.
isle_of_contemplation.mystery: The sundial's gnomon is filed to a stub. A hermit counts the bells of Alinor from here and says one is missing from the day's twenty-four.
clues: a sundial with its gnomon filed down
tally marks of sixty years of dusk
a hermit's cup beside a single empty chair
isle_of_contemplation.payoff: The hermit's bell-tally, with sixty years of dusk counted.
isle_of_contemplation.rumour: The hermit on the Isle of Contemplation counts twenty-three bells every dusk and swears there should be twenty-four.

colosseum_of_the_old_ways.name: Colosseum of the Old Ways
colosseum_of_the_old_ways.site: A ruined ring arena on Artaeum's shore, its floor a pale mosaic of hours and its tiers half-sunk in sand.
colosseum_of_the_old_ways.mystery: The mosaic of hours shows twenty-three. One tile has been pried out and replaced by a patch of bare grey stone. A match was held in that hour, and no one remembers who won.
clues: a mosaic with a bare grey tile at the twenty-fourth place
a sand floor with a scuff-ring around a fighter's stance
a trophy-stand with one empty pedestal
colosseum_of_the_old_ways.payoff: The pried-out tile's edge-pattern, a rubbing to match a missing door.
colosseum_of_the_old_ways.rumour: The Old Ways arena's floor has a grey tile where an hour should be. Nobody remembers the fight that was held there.

alinor.name: Alinor
alinor.site: A radial city of quartz with a Crystal Tower at the hub, sixteen avenues and a palace on a terrace.
alinor.mystery: The city's bell-tower chimes twenty-three each dusk, and its clock has a blank face at the twenty-fourth. The bell-ringer was dismissed for asking.
clues: a clock-face with a blank at the twenty-fourth
a bell-ringer's dismissal notice nailed to the tower door
chimes that pause one beat too long at dusk
alinor.payoff: The bell-ringer's warding-word, which opens the vault of false doors.

traitors_vault.name: Traitor's Vault
traitors_vault.site: A vault of false doors on Artaeum where each room offers three exits, two of which loop back through mirrors.
traitors_vault.mystery: The vault was built to hold evidence of an act that the Order erased. The true vault lies behind a wall that must be broken, and the gold on show is bait.
clues: rooms with three doors and two mirrors
a wall with a hairline crack of cold light
treasure chests trapped and empty
traitors_vault.payoff: The true vault's brick, a key for the tower's lens-door.
traitors_vault.rumour: The Traitor's Vault has more doors than rooms. The ones that open lead to the same place.

crystal_tower_summerset.name: Crystal Tower
crystal_tower_summerset.site: A needle of crystal many times taller than anything, glowing at night, with a spiral of lens-rooms at its summit.
crystal_tower_summerset.mystery: The tower's summit lens refracts the hours. One of its panes shows the skipped hour as a faint ghost room. The tower's wardens keep it covered with a cloth.
clues: a lens-room pane covered by a cloth
a clock-face on the stair with no hands
a wardens' register missing a single page
crystal_tower_summerset.payoff: A ghost-lens that shows the hour as a room.
crystal_tower_summerset.rumour: The Crystal Tower's summit lenses were covered with a cloth at the spring equinox. The wardens won't say what they saw before they did it.
crystal_tower_summerset.thread_clue: a lens-room whose lenses face the sky at the wrong angle

psijic_relic_vaults.name: Psijic Relic Vaults
psijic_relic_vaults.site: A vault of sliding walls and phase-doors where rooms rearrange as you move and time-eddies freeze torches.
psijic_relic_vaults.mystery: The skipped hour is a room in this vault that rearranges to hide itself. In it, a candle burns on a table beside a stopped clock and a hand reaching for a cup.
clues: a room whose candle burns without shortening
a clock stopped at the twenty-fourth hour
a hand-print in dust on a cup that was never lifted
psijic_relic_vaults.payoff: A unique relic: the skipped hour itself, a candle that returns an hour.
psijic_relic_vaults.rumour: The Psijic vaults move their rooms. Folk say there is one that has been moved so often it is no longer anywhere.
psijic_relic_vaults.thread_clue: a vault door open for the first time in a thousand years

dawnbreak.name: Dawnbreak
dawnbreak.site: A hamlet on an Auridon bluff above the sea, with white cottages and a row of weathered crosses of crystal.
dawnbreak.mystery: A villager's grave is scattered with crystal splinters. The villagers say the fever starts as a glint in the eye and ends with a walk into the sea.
clues: a grave scattered with fine crystal splinters
cottages with glass shards pressed in the window sills
a child's chalk drawing of a glittering eye
dawnbreak.payoff: A glint-ward amulet, a crude shield against the fever.
dawnbreak.rumour: At Dawnbreak a man walked into the sea last winter. His eyes shone like cut glass the week before.

maras_kiss_public_house.name: Mara's Kiss Public House
maras_kiss_public_house.site: A bright tavern on the Auridon road with a garden of fruit trees, a lantern for each drinker and a wide stone hearth.
maras_kiss_public_house.mystery: The fever first showed in the tavern's customers. The innkeeper traced it to a barrel of cider pressed from Shattered Grove apples. The apples glittered.
clues: a cider barrel with a seam of crystal along the stave
lantern-glass fractured in a spiderweb
a drinker's cup with a splinter in the dregs
maras_kiss_public_house.payoff: A sealed cider-sample and a map of the grove.
maras_kiss_public_house.rumour: Mara's Kiss serves a cider that sparkles on the tongue. They stopped pouring it after the second drinker went quiet.

shattered_grove.name: Shattered Grove
shattered_grove.site: A grove of splintered crystal trees in Auridon, their bark cracked and the fallen fruit sparkling in the grass.
shattered_grove.mystery: The grove is a Daedric seed that took root in a lightning-struck ash. The crystals are not stone but patient teeth, and each fruit holds a thread of the cult's whisper.
clues: bark cracked into glassy shards
fruit that glitters but bruises like flesh
a ring of villagers' footprints that end at a root
shattered_grove.payoff: A grove-shard that responds to the seed's heart.
shattered_grove.rumour: The Shattered Grove bore the largest fruit of its life this year. The folk who ate it have all begun to glitter.

firsthold.name: Firsthold
firsthold.site: A white-walled tidal port of Auridon where every ship from the mainland must anchor under the eye of a lighthouse.
firsthold.mystery: The harbour-master has been quietly turning away ships carrying glittering passengers, who then come ashore in boats at night.
clues: a harbour-master's quarantine list
night-boats with unlit lanterns
a ward-line of salt along the quay
firsthold.payoff: The harbour-master's quarantine list of the glittering.
firsthold.thread_clue: a lens-case with a page folded under the glass

skywatch.name: Skywatch
skywatch.site: A hill-city topped by a vast ring-orrery with concentric stone ring-walks and observatories on each ring.
skywatch.mystery: The star-watchers calculate that the seed's heart will awaken at a conjunction nine weeks hence. A cult has been tilting the orrery to bring it sooner.
clues: an orrery ring out of true by a degree
a star-watcher's calculation scrawled on a wall
cult marks on the lowest ring's underside
skywatch.payoff: The conjunction date and the cult's bearing.
skywatch.rumour: The great orrery at Skywatch was tilted by a degree one night, and the star-watchers can't say by whom. The conjunction comes sooner now.

the_banished_cells.name: The Banished Cells
the_banished_cells.site: A Daedric prison under a spire with cell-blocks of obsidian, chains and windows on nothing.
the_banished_cells.mystery: The cult's refusers are held here, the glass-fevered who would not walk to the sea. Their splinters grow inward, and they are lucid.
clues: cells of obsidian with names scratched on the bars
a prisoner who glitters but speaks in full sentences
windows that open on a red sky
the_banished_cells.payoff: A prisoner's testimony and a key to the red fortress.
the_banished_cells.rumour: A prison under a spire holds those who said no to the fever. They are asking to be let out and they are right.

mehrunes_spite.name: Mehrunes' Spite
mehrunes_spite.site: A red-spired fortress of Dagon's cult with lava channels around a central court, spike gardens and a ritual hall under a brazier-crown.
mehrunes_spite.mystery: The seed-crystal stands in the ritual hall like a throne. The cult's prophet believes it a seed of a new world. It is a seed of an old one.
clues: a crystal throne in a ritual hall
spike gardens of glass-bladed flowers
braziers lit with blue flame
mehrunes_spite.payoff: The seed-crystal's heart: a unique crystal that heals glass-fever.
mehrunes_spite.rumour: A red fortress on the Auridon cliffs has a hall where a crystal hums. The cult say it is the future. The grove says otherwise.

kings_haven.name: King's Haven
kings_haven.site: A small keep and orchard on the Summerset coast, with a reeve's house and a walled egg-yard where gryphon clutches were once gathered.
kings_haven.mystery: The reeve's ledger lists thirty clutches a season forwarded to Cloudrest, then none this spring. He suspects the steward has been selling them and says so to anyone who will listen.
clues: an egg-yard with empty straw nests
a ledger's tithe column with a ruled-off blank
gryphon feathers in the orchard grass, none fresh
kings_haven.payoff: The reeve's ledger of eggs sent and unaccounted for.
kings_haven.rumour: The reeve at King's Haven swears the gryphons have stopped laying and then tells you he doesn't believe it.

the_golden_netch.name: The Golden Netch
the_golden_netch.site: An inn under a gilded netch-balloon on the Summerset coast road with a rope-ladder entrance and a wide kitchen.
the_golden_netch.mystery: A dealer has lodged here for a week, leaving each night with a heavy crate. The innkeeper says the crate clinked and was warm.
clues: a warm crate on the dealer's cart
straw on the stair that smells of gryphon
a bill of lading with the steward's seal
the_golden_netch.payoff: The dealer's bill of lading, naming the port.
the_golden_netch.rumour: A dealer at the Golden Netch pays for his room in coin and his crates in silence. The crates are warm.

shimmerene.name: Shimmerene
shimmerene.site: A busy port on a bay with dockside lanterns on high poles, long wharves and crane-masts.
shimmerene.mystery: The harbour has a quiet quay where crates marked 'minerals' are loaded for a foreign ship at night. A customs man looks away.
clues: crates marked 'minerals' that tick softly
a quiet quay with no lantern
a customs man's palm freshly gilded
shimmerene.payoff: A stolen clutch recovered from the quiet quay.
shimmerene.rumour: The quiet quay at Shimmerene has no lantern, and crates marked 'minerals' go aboard a foreign ship after dark. The customs man looks away.

gryphon_aerie.name: Gryphon Aerie
gryphon_aerie.site: A cliff nest of enormous gryphons on the Summerset coast, ledges of straw and wind-scoured stone.
gryphon_aerie.mystery: The nesting ledges are empty. The mother gryphons circle, calling for their clutches. Their song, which should hold up a palace, has dwindled to a thread.
clues: empty nests on a cliff of fresh feathers
mother gryphons calling in a thin note
a climbing rope left by the thieves
gryphon_aerie.payoff: The recovered clutch, and the mother's song.
gryphon_aerie.rumour: The gryphons at the aerie have started calling at night, and their calls are shorter than they used to be.

cloudrest.name: Cloudrest
cloudrest.site: A palace-city on a sea cliff with cantilevered balconies over open air, glass floors and no walls.
cloudrest.mystery: The balconies' stone ticks in the dark. The steward has been quietly shoring up the lower rooms with iron to hide the fault.
clues: iron braces bolted under a balcony
a glass floor with a hairline crack
a steward's strongbox full of Pyandonean coin
cloudrest.payoff: The steward's strongbox ledger, proof of the egg sales.
cloudrest.rumour: Cloudrest hangs its balconies over open air. The steward has been shoring the lower ones with iron where the courtiers will not see.

tor_hame_khard.name: Tor Hame Khard
tor_hame_khard.site: A crystal fortress carved into a sea cliff with sea-gates at wave level, a waterfall court and a lightning-rod tower.
tor_hame_khard.mystery: The lightning-rod tower is an amplifier for the gryphons' song, tuned to the palace above. Without a clutch to hatch in its warm court, it falls silent.
clues: a lightning rod that hums in the key of a gryphon
a warm court with an empty brooding-floor
waterfall steps lit by tuned crystals
tor_hame_khard.payoff: A tuning-fork of the song: a unique that steadies Cloudrest's stones.
tor_hame_khard.rumour: The fortress's tower hums at storm-time in a voice like a very large bird.
tor_hame_khard.thread_clue: a waterfall court whose cascade is silent for one hour each night

trebbite_monastery.name: Trebbite Monastery
trebbite_monastery.site: A small monastery on the Auridon coast with a cloister of white stone, a silent refectory and an urn of silk spools.
trebbite_monastery.mystery: The monks found silk with words in it caught in their orchard. They think a spider is writing and fear it is a blessing.
clues: an urn of spools wound around tiny slips
a refectory with a web across one wall
monks who whisper the words they find
trebbite_monastery.payoff: The spools' first words: a list of lost titles.
trebbite_monastery.rumour: The Trebbite brothers have found silk in the orchard with words woven in it. They say please don't eat it.

dusk.name: Dusk
dusk.site: A crescent harbour city under pale dunes, lilac in the evening, with a tall lantern tower and pastel houses.
dusk.mystery: Library-barges from Lillandril dock here by night with sealed crates marked 'water-damaged'. The books inside are blank.
clues: crates of blank books on the quay
a lantern tower lit lilac at dusk
a bookbinder's shop with empty covers in the window
dusk.payoff: A blank book, proof the words have been taken.
dusk.rumour: Book-barges come into Dusk at night with cargo that's all blank paper. The bookbinders are doing a brisk trade in covers.

lillandril.name: Lillandril
lillandril.site: A city of terraced libraries and observatories on a rock, with ring galleries of book-stacks open to the sky and bronze orreries.
lillandril.mystery: A third of the stacks are blank and the head librarian has gone missing. A librarian's assistant claims to hear reading from beyond the cliff.
clues: stacks with blank spines
a head librarian's empty chair and half-eaten supper
a gallery window with a web spun across it
lillandril.payoff: The head librarian's last catalogue entry, a bearing to the acropolis.
lillandril.rumour: A third of Lillandril's stacks are blank, and the head librarian has gone missing. The assistants say they can hear reading from beyond the cliff.

direnni_acropolis.name: Direnni Acropolis
direnni_acropolis.site: A ruined hilltop acropolis of white columns, a stage of marble and a high cistern of black water.
direnni_acropolis.mystery: The acropolis is where the spiders first came to read, drawn by an echo in the cistern. Their webs span every column.
clues: columns webbed from base to capital
a cistern whose surface carries letters
a lectern with a book that is open to a page of silk
direnni_acropolis.payoff: A silk-page that lets its reader hear the vault's reading.
direnni_acropolis.rumour: The old acropolis has webs across every column, and some say you can hear a voice reading in them.

cathedral_of_webs.name: Cathedral of Webs
cathedral_of_webs.site: A crystal vault wrapped in giant spider-silk, shafts of light through white webs onto lecterns of woven thread.
cathedral_of_webs.mystery: The missing librarian sits at a silk-lectern reading to a roomful of patient spiders, and has been for months. She says it is the finest audience she has ever had.
clues: lecterns of woven thread with open silk-books
a librarian's cup refilled by no one
spiders arranged in tiers like a congregation
cathedral_of_webs.payoff: The Silk Library's catalogue: a unique tome that restores a lost book.
cathedral_of_webs.rumour: The Cathedral of Webs is a place of reading. The spiders sit very still.

stay_moist_mansion.name: Stay-Moist Mansion
stay_moist_mansion.site: A merchant's stilt mansion in the Stormhold marsh with a boat-shed, a bright awning and a lantern-lit veranda.
stay_moist_mansion.mystery: The merchant sells sap to Imperial pharmacists. His storehouse is full of casks stamped with a golden sun, though the Hist should not be tapped.
clues: casks stamped with a sun and a tally
a boat-shed with a sap-pump on its dock
a veranda lantern that burns green sap
stay_moist_mansion.payoff: A sap-cask seal, proof the root is being sold.
stay_moist_mansion.rumour: The merchant at Stay-Moist has more sap than a thousand trees could give, and he sells it by the cask to the Imperials.

xal_haj_ei_shrine.name: Xal Haj-Ei Shrine
xal_haj_ei_shrine.site: A shrine in a hollow reed-forest, half-sunk in a pool, its walls carved with root-patterns.
xal_haj_ei_shrine.mystery: The shrine's pool is a mouth of the Root. Its water has turned grey, and the shrine-keepers weep at dawn.
clues: a pool grey as ash in the shrine's heart
root-carvings with chiselled gaps
keepers' drums stilled and wrapped in cloth
xal_haj_ei_shrine.payoff: A shrine-keeper's tear-vial, an offering that can lull the falls.
xal_haj_ei_shrine.rumour: The shrine in the reeds has gone grey. The keepers say the Root is in pain.

weeping_wamasu_falls.name: Weeping Wamasu Falls
weeping_wamasu_falls.site: A high waterfall with the shape of a giant weeping creature carved into the rock behind its sheet.
weeping_wamasu_falls.mystery: The falls' note has sunk to a whisper this season. The wamasu in the rock is losing its voice, and the Argonians say the Root is the throat of the world.
clues: a waterfall with its note gone thin
a rock face where tear-lines have dried
offerings of reeds at the base, withered
weeping_wamasu_falls.payoff: A wamasu-tear, a drop that changes tone when near a tapped root.
weeping_wamasu_falls.rumour: The Weeping Wamasu has fallen quiet. The Argonians say it is losing its voice because the marsh has a cut in it.
weeping_wamasu_falls.thread_clue: a falls whose note has thinned to a whisper

stormhold.name: Stormhold
stormhold.site: A fortress city of two stepped ziggurats on facing hills, joined by a long bridge across a gorge.
stormhold.mystery: The Imperial pharmacists' guild has an office at the river gate. Its sap manifest is bound in a ledger that is not allowed to be photographed or copied.
clues: a pharmacists' office with a locked ledger
river-gate crates stamped with a sun
a bridge guard with a sap-sweetened breath
stormhold.payoff: The pharmacists' manifest, naming the buyers and the amounts.

temple_of_sul.name: Temple of Sul
temple_of_sul.site: A sun-temple with bright shafts and a gold altar, its roof carved to focus a single beam at noon.
temple_of_sul.mystery: The merchant's sun-stamp is borrowed from this temple. A corrupt priest sold the temple's mark and a licence for sap-gathering, and the altar's gold is his payment.
clues: a gold altar with a priest's footprints in the dust
a roof beam that falls on the wrong spot
a licence-plate stamped with a sun
temple_of_sul.payoff: A temple licence that exposes the corrupt priest.
temple_of_sul.rumour: The Temple of Sul's gold is real, but the priest who kept it hasn't prayed in a year.

bogmother.name: Bogmother
bogmother.site: A fetid root-cave and hag-lair where a mother-of-bog spawns, with walls of knotted root and a dripping ceiling.
bogmother.mystery: The hag is the Root's antibody: each time the tap is drawn she spawns a clutch of guardians. The more sap is drawn, the more she must bear.
clues: knotted root-walls weeping green
spawn-clutches in every alcove
a tap-pipe running in through the ceiling
bogmother.payoff: A hag's root-knot that quiets her spawn.
bogmother.rumour: Something big has been laying in the swamp lately. The hunters won't go past the bend.

shrine_of_the_black_maw.name: Shrine of the Black Maw
shrine_of_the_black_maw.site: A sacred shrine built into a gaping rock mouth with processional halls and a great black pool.
shrine_of_the_black_maw.mystery: The pool is the Root's mouth, where it drinks the dead's names. The tap's other end is here, a brass fitting driven into the pool's bottom.
clues: a brass fitting driven into the black pool
processional halls wet with sap
a pool whose surface shows the faces of the dead
shrine_of_the_black_maw.payoff: The tap-fitting itself, and a unique Hist fang that heals what was cut.
shrine_of_the_black_maw.rumour: The Black Maw's pool has a metal thing in it now. The shrine-keepers say it is a thorn in the world's tongue.

hatchlings_crown.name: Hatchling's Crown
hatchlings_crown.site: A hill crowned with a ring of egg-shaped stones near Lilmoth, each carved with a notch-count of warmth.
hatchlings_crown.mystery: The stones hold the warm-count of every season. The latest notch is the deepest cut: the heat has fallen by a degree.
clues: egg-shaped stones with notch-counts
a deep new notch chiselled this week
a keeper's string of pale eggshells
hatchlings_crown.rumour: The egg-stones of the crown measure the warmth of the pools. The last cut is the deepest anyone has seen.

hatching_pools.name: Hatching Pools
hatching_pools.site: A ring of warm pools in Stormhold's lowland, each steaming faintly with a clutch in a nest of reeds.
hatching_pools.mystery: The pools are cooler by a degree each year, and the hatchlings come pale and weak. Steam rises from the pools toward the southern mire instead of upward.
clues: steam trailing south in a single thread
pale hatchlings at the pool edge
keepers wrapping eggs in warmed cloth
hatching_pools.payoff: A steam-vial that shows the direction of the stolen heat.
hatching_pools.rumour: The hatching pools are cooler. The steam goes south in a thread, and the keepers follow it with their eyes.

lilmoth.name: Lilmoth
lilmoth.site: A delta city on stilts with canals instead of streets, hundreds of boats and a ziggurat over a market of woven mats.
lilmoth.mystery: The ziggurat's lowest cistern is cold, and has been for a year. The priest-keepers say something draws on it from underneath.
clues: a cold cistern in a warm ziggurat
a fishmonger's catch frozen where it should be fresh
a thread of steam that trails south-east
lilmoth.payoff: A priest-keeper's chart of the cold's direction.

the_vile_pavilion.name: The Vile Pavilion
the_vile_pavilion.site: A rotting banquet pavilion on the mire with floating platforms joined by plank walks and a long table with plates that still steam.
the_vile_pavilion.mystery: The plates steam because the pavilion's lord draws the pools' heat. He thinks you are late for dinner. His guests cannot leave until the supper ends.
clues: a long table with steaming plates
guests seated, unmoving, ankle-deep in mire
a lord's chair with a cold hearth behind it
the_vile_pavilion.payoff: The lord's carving knife, a unique that draws heat or cold.
the_vile_pavilion.rumour: A pavilion in the mire has food that steams on a night with frost. Nobody who sits there has returned for dessert.

jeevu_rice_paddy.name: Jeevu Rice Paddy
jeevu_rice_paddy.site: A rice paddy in the Shadowfen, with rows of seedlings in black water and a harvest-counter's high chair.
jeevu_rice_paddy.mystery: The counter's tally has an extra worker each dusk. The evening bowl is set out by habit for a person nobody can name.
clues: a tally sheet with one extra worker each dusk
a bowl set at the end of the field
a row of seedlings planted by someone no one saw
jeevu_rice_paddy.payoff: The counter's tally of the extra one.
jeevu_rice_paddy.rumour: The rice-counter at Jeevu counts forty-two at dusk where there were forty-one at dawn. She doesn't like it.

root_whisper_village.name: Root Whisper Village
root_whisper_village.site: An abandoned Hist-village, huts overgrown with root-vine and a central fire-pit still warm at the edges.
root_whisper_village.mystery: The village fled when the Hist spoke a name no one knew, and every bowl was set for one more. The roots have grown through the walls to the table.
clues: a long table with a chair at the head no one will sit in
roots grown through the walls reaching the table
a fire-pit warm at dawn
root_whisper_village.payoff: A speaker-reed that records the Hist's whisper.
root_whisper_village.rumour: Root Whisper's folk left in a night. The roots have grown into their huts and their table has a chair that stays warm.
root_whisper_village.thread_clue: a root-chair where ash has settled in the shape of a person

thorn.name: Thorn
thorn.site: A hub of a single enormous Hist tree whose roots carry walkways, huts hung from the roots, a pool at the base and sap-lanterns.
thorn.mystery: The pool's reflection shows a figure who is not a villager, seated at the back of the crowd at festivals. The Hist-sages say it is a guest of the Hist.
clues: a reflection in the pool of a figure at the back
a festival-seat left empty at the rear of the crowd
a sap-lantern that burns blue when the figure is near
thorn.payoff: A reflection-bowl that shows the figure's face.
thorn.rumour: The great pool at Thorn shows a figure at the back of every festival crowd that nobody can name.
thorn.thread_clue: a pool whose surface takes ash and holds a ghost of it

helstrom.name: Helstrom
helstrom.site: A border town on the edge of the Shadowfen, with new stilt-houses grown among broken monoliths and rope walkways.
helstrom.mystery: The border-post's tally always has one more than the roll. The captain has stopped correcting it and writes 'plus one' in his book.
clues: a border-post book with 'plus one' in the margin
a gate whose latch opens by itself at dusk
monoliths carved with a name no one can read
helstrom.payoff: The captain's roll with 'plus one' and the monoliths' inscription.
helstrom.thread_clue: a border-post whose ash-drifts always cross in one direction

ruins_of_mazzatun.name: Ruins of Mazzatun
ruins_of_mazzatun.site: A xanmeer of stepped chambers where the floor is a flooded city, with sap-vein walls and a central shaft.
ruins_of_mazzatun.mystery: At the bottom of the shaft sits a figure who does not breathe. It is the village's founder, never named, who counts the water as it rises. He wishes only to be named.
clues: a seated figure at the bottom of the shaft
walls with sap-veins that pulse in sequence
a bowl set at the water's edge, still warm
ruins_of_mazzatun.payoff: The founder's name, and a unique that calms a restless shade.
ruins_of_mazzatun.rumour: Mazzatun's flood rises a hand per year. Folk say a quiet figure sits at the bottom and counts.

hutan_tzel.name: Hutan Tzel
hutan_tzel.site: A fishing hamlet on the southern delta, with drying racks and a graveyard whose markers are wooden reeds.
hutan_tzel.mystery: The graves are moved inland every year, because the dirge no longer goes to the water. The singers say the path was moved by a hand with money.
clues: grave-markers moved a hundred paces inland
drying-racks hung with mourning ribbons
a fisher's empty chair at the water's edge
hutan_tzel.payoff: A mourning-ribbon braid that opens the singers' lodge.
hutan_tzel.rumour: At Hutan Tzel the dead are buried inland, now. The singers don't sing them to the water.

grave_singers_lodge.name: Grave Singers' Lodge
grave_singers_lodge.site: A lodge of singers on a hummock in the delta, hung with reed-chimes, with a single long table of seven empty chairs.
grave_singers_lodge.mystery: The singers' choir has dwindled to three. Four were bribed to sing the new route, and they have not sung since. The three keep the old verse.
clues: seven chairs at a table, four dusty
a verse tablet with a line crossed out and rewritten
reed-chimes bound with a coin-string
grave_singers_lodge.payoff: The old verse's final line and a map of the dirge's new route.
grave_singers_lodge.rumour: The singers' lodge has seven chairs and three singers. The other four have taken the lord's coin.

plateau_of_the_traveler.name: Plateau of the Traveler
plateau_of_the_traveler.site: A lone rock plateau with a view across the delta and a flat stone, polished by feet, at its edge.
plateau_of_the_traveler.mystery: From the plateau's edge the dirge's old path is a silver thread to the sea. The new path is a dark scar through the dry fields.
clues: a polished flat stone at the plateau's edge
a silver thread across the delta at dusk
a dark scar through the fields beyond
plateau_of_the_traveler.payoff: A surveyor's sighting of the dirge's two routes.
plateau_of_the_traveler.rumour: From the lone plateau you can see two paths. One is silver, one is dark. Choose carefully which you follow.

gideon.name: Gideon
gideon.site: A walled plateau town in the drier east of the delta with rings of terraced clay houses and a high watchtower.
gideon.mystery: The plantation lord's courtyard holds stacked coffins waiting to be sung over. He believes the dead's blessing will bring rain.
clues: a courtyard of waiting coffins
