a watchtower with a bell silent for years
a well half-dry with a ring of white salt
gideon.payoff: A lord's contract with the four bribed singers.

soulrest.name: Soulrest
soulrest.site: A necropolis island city of stilt-house rows, canals, white lily beds and bone-barges.
soulrest.mystery: The island's quiet has been broken: no bone-barge has docked in a year. The island's keepers watch the delta for the dirge and see nothing.
clues: empty bone-barges at their moorings
lily beds withering for want of the dead's warmth
a watch-bell rung nightly with no answer
soulrest.payoff: A keeper's chart of the dirge's true end, in the mire.
soulrest.rumour: No bone-barge has docked at Soulrest in a year, and the island's keepers watch the delta for a dirge that does not come.
soulrest.thread_clue: a crypt-door unlocked with a key-shaped scar in its lintel

murkmire.name: Murkmire
murkmire.site: A remote hut spiral in the deep mire with a path winding to the centre fire, mist and croaks.
murkmire.mystery: The huts' spiral points to a ring of teeth in the mire where the dirge ends. The villagers sing the last verse alone each night.
clues: huts arranged in a spiral toward the mire's heart
a fire that burns with no smoke
a night-chant of a single voice
murkmire.payoff: The last verse of the dirge, sung to the teeth.

teeth_of_sithis.name: Teeth of Sithis
teeth_of_sithis.site: A ring of black teeth rising from the mire around a sunken hollow, with root paths between each tooth, each tooth a different trial.
teeth_of_sithis.mystery: The dirge ends in the hollow's centre, where the dead's songs are laid. The rerouted dirge has left it silent, and the hollow has begun to sink.
clues: black teeth ringed around a sunken hollow
root paths between each tooth
a sinking centre where the song should rest
teeth_of_sithis.payoff: The final verse's key: a unique mace that calls the dead's song.
teeth_of_sithis.rumour: The ring of teeth is quiet. The old folk say it used to sing.

saarvik_landing.name: Saarvik Landing
saarvik_landing.site: A landing of broken ships on an Atmoran shore, ribs and masts half-buried in drifts, a single cairn at the tide line.
saarvik_landing.mystery: A dead sailor kneels in the wreckage clutching a rune-tablet that warns of the ice. The tablet is fresh to the touch.
clues: ship's ribs frosted over a tablet
a cairn with a warning rune
a boat-ramp cracked by a seam of ice
saarvik_landing.payoff: The rune-tablet: a warning and a map of the hold.
saarvik_landing.rumour: At Saarvik the ships sit in drifts, and the cairn's rune glows when the ice speaks.

skjaldborg.name: Skjaldborg
skjaldborg.site: A shield-fort on the Atmoran ice, its wall a ring of battered shields and a single hall of frosted wood.
skjaldborg.mystery: The fort's shield-wall has been rearranged: each shield now faces the ice shelf. The garrison's captain says the shields remember what they once guarded.
clues: shields all turned toward the ice shelf
a hall of frosted wood with a hearth cold for a decade
a captain's log with all pages blank but one
skjaldborg.payoff: The captain's last page: a call to the hold.
skjaldborg.rumour: The shields at Skjaldborg all face the ice now. The captain won't say who turned them.

kjolvik.name: Kjolvik
kjolvik.site: A last Atmoran hold on an ice shelf with ten long halls half-buried in drifts, whale-bone arches and a stone-lined harbour where ice cracks.
kjolvik.mystery: The ice is cracking beneath the halls. The elders deny it and sing in the long hall, drowning out the groan. The children carry the news.
clues: a harbour where ice splits at night
elders singing against the groan
children's sledges loaded with winter-stores for a journey
kjolvik.payoff: A hold-token that persuades the mound's wardens.
kjolvik.rumour: Kjolvik's elders sing in the long hall at night, loudly, so the ice cannot be heard. The children ask to be taught the old ship-songs.

the_frozen_dragon_mound.name: The Frozen Dragon Mound
the_frozen_dragon_mound.site: A mound of ice with a dragon's head frozen at its crown, jaws open in a final roar.
the_frozen_dragon_mound.mystery: The dragon is the pin of the ice shelf: its cold keeps the seam bound. It has begun to thaw at the throat, and the seam answers.
clues: a dragon's head dripping from the throat
a seam running from the mound out to sea
a ring of stones where chiefs once swore
the_frozen_dragon_mound.payoff: A shard of the dragon's cold, which can hold the seam a season.
the_frozen_dragon_mound.rumour: The frozen dragon has begun to weep at the throat, and the ice-seam under the halls is following it.
the_frozen_dragon_mound.thread_clue: a frozen throat with a clean hole where a vertebra should be

wolf_jarls_howe.name: Wolf-Jarl's Howe
wolf_jarls_howe.site: A great Atmoran barrow under a hill of snow with a long ship buried whole as the dungeon's central room.
wolf_jarls_howe.mystery: The burial ship waits for its captain, sealed with oaths. The wolf-jarl's ghost has guarded her for a thousand years and will release her only to one who speaks the word the hold has forgotten.
clues: a long ship's prow rising from the central hall
a ghost-captain at the helm
ropes frozen taut to the barrow's walls
wolf_jarls_howe.payoff: The ship's release and the wolf-jarl's axe: a unique Atmoran frostaxe.
wolf_jarls_howe.rumour: The howe's ship is whole. They say you can hear her creak in the dark of the barrow.
wolf_jarls_howe.thread_clue: a keel-chest with its lock sprung and its lid ajar

tang_mo_watch.name: Tang Mo Watch
tang_mo_watch.site: A border watchtower on the Tang Mo coast with a lantern at its crown and a stone at its foot carved with a fourfold seal.
tang_mo_watch.mystery: Pilgrims rub the border stone smooth, and the fourth quarter is the only one that has not worn. The guards say it is cold to the touch, even in summer.
clues: a border stone with three worn quarters and one fresh
pilgrim sandals left in a row at the foot
a lantern lit by day
tang_mo_watch.payoff: A rubbing of the stone's fourfold seal.
tang_mo_watch.rumour: The watchmen say the border stone has been rubbed smooth by pilgrims, all but one corner that stays cold.

tang_mo_harbor_village.name: Tang Mo Harbor Village
tang_mo_harbor_village.site: A harbour of lacquered junks and floating lantern-masts, houses raised on bamboo piles with curved roofs and a dragon-prowed ship at the quay.
tang_mo_harbor_village.mystery: The harbour keeps one quarter of the seal inside the dragon-prow: a jade tablet that glows when the tide is high.
clues: a jade tablet glowing in the dragon-prow
lantern-masts lit in a pattern of four
a ferryman with a seal's quarter tattooed on his palm
tang_mo_harbor_village.payoff: The harbour's quarter of the seal.
tang_mo_harbor_village.rumour: The dragon-prow at Tang Mo's quay has a jade tablet set in its throat that glows when the tide is high. The ferrymen have a seal tattooed on their palms.

tiger_plains_village.name: Tiger Plains Village
tiger_plains_village.site: A mountain village of curved-roof pagodas on rice terraces with a vermilion shrine gate, bamboo and paper lanterns.
tiger_plains_village.mystery: The village keeps a second quarter in a lantern that never goes out. The headman says it is a family heirloom; he does not say whose family.
clues: a lantern that burns in the rain
a vermilion gate with a quarter-seal in its lintel
paper lanterns painted with four courts
tiger_plains_village.payoff: The village's quarter of the seal.
tiger_plains_village.rumour: A lantern in the headman's house at Tiger Plains has burned without oil since before the village had a name, and he says it is a family heirloom.

temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.name: Temple of the Serpent Emperor
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.site: A tall serpent-roofed temple on a Tsaesci ridge, with coils of painted stair and a bell-gate at the summit.
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.mystery: The Tsaesci hold the third quarter and want the fourth. Their priests wait patiently on the ridge, coiled in the temple's shadow.
clues: coiled stair carved with a countdown
priests who bow but do not speak
a bell-gate with a missing clapper
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.payoff: The third quarter and a ridge-path to the valley.
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.rumour: The serpent-priests wait. They wait without hurry, and they are not the ones who fear.
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.thread_clue: a cradle of vertebrae two short of its full length

dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.name: Dragon Graveyard of Akavir
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.site: A valley floor of enormous ribcages, white as salt under a low sky, with a path of vertebrae winding between them.
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.mystery: The dragons died here by choice. Each ribcage points to the ice throne. The valley groans when the seal is touched.
clues: ribcages all open toward the north
a path of vertebrae worn smooth
a groan when the wind drops
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.payoff: A rib-key which opens the ice throne's hall.
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.rumour: The valley of ribs groans at dusk. The Akaviri say it is the dragons turning over in their sleep.
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.thread_clue: a ribcage whose spine has a gap exactly one vertebra wide

frost_throne_of_kamal.name: Frost Throne of Kamal
frost_throne_of_kamal.site: A throne-hall of ice and iron with a giant ice throne in a hall of ice pagodas.
frost_throne_of_kamal.mystery: The fourth quarter is set in the throne's arm. A frost-warden sits on the throne in a cold that does not melt. He guards against the day the seal is joined.
clues: a throne with a socket in its arm
ice pagodas with names frozen inside
a warden whose breath makes no cloud
frost_throne_of_kamal.payoff: The fourth quarter, completing the seal: a unique shehai that cuts frost.
frost_throne_of_kamal.rumour: The throne of Kamal is cold even in summer. The frost-warden has not blinked in a thousand years.
frost_throne_of_kamal.thread_clue: a throne-arm with a socket shaped like a ring

serpent_pens.name: Serpent Pens
serpent_pens.site: A serpent pen of coral-walled pools on a Maormer isle, with feeding platforms and pole-and-net gates.
serpent_pens.mystery: The serpents have been feeding on pink coral drifted in from the south, and have swollen strangely. Some pens have burst.
clues: a pen-gate of netting torn from within
pink coral rooted in the pole-gates
serpents bloated and slow, scales gone pink at the edges
serpent_pens.payoff: A pink coral-shard: proof the reef is spreading.
serpent_pens.rumour: The serpents at the pens eat a pink weed and grow, and one pen has already burst. The keepers don't speak of it.
serpent_pens.thread_clue: a keeper's totem with a page rolled into its hollow

pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.name: Pyandonean Fleet Anchorage
pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.site: A fleet at anchor, a raft-city of shell-hulled ships lashed together, a coral flagship and serpent-prowed boats, gleaming wet.
pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.mystery: The fleet's captains have noticed the reef drifts closer each tide. The flagship has begun to drag its anchor. The admiral keeps the chart secret.
clues: lashings re-tied nightly against drift
a flagship's anchor chain taut
an admiral's chart with a pink line that crosses the fleet
pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.payoff: The admiral's drift-chart: the reef's path.
pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.rumour: The shell-hulled fleet at anchor keeps pulling south against its lashings. The admiral says it is the current. The deck-hands do not.

coral_tower_of_thras.name: Coral Tower of Thras
coral_tower_of_thras.site: A tower of living coral in a sea of plague, with rooms of pulsing polyps, bright pink and poison green and a spiral reef stair.
coral_tower_of_thras.mystery: The tower is the reef's head: it grows a fathom a year and sends its spawn to drift. The tower's heart-chamber is a nursery of coral.
clues: rooms of pulsing polyps
a spiral stair with each step a coral-shell
a heart-chamber that beats once a minute
coral_tower_of_thras.payoff: A coral-heart: a unique that can kill or call a reef.
coral_tower_of_thras.rumour: The tower in the plague sea has grown a fathom this year. The folk of Thras say it is thinking.

orgnums_citadel.name: Orgnum's Citadel
orgnums_citadel.site: A sea-serpent citadel on a crag with boat-lifts, brine tanks, serpent pens and a throne hall with a window onto the deep.
orgnums_citadel.mystery: The throne hall's window faces the reef's head. The sea-king has been staring at it for a year, and has not slept. He cannot decide whether to kill it or crown it.
clues: a throne hall whose window is filled with pink
a king's chair with an untouched cup
boat-lifts rusted from disuse
orgnums_citadel.payoff: A sea-gate key that shuts the reef out of the citadel's waters.
orgnums_citadel.rumour: The sea-king stares into the deep and will not eat. The court says he is waiting for it to blink.
orgnums_citadel.thread_clue: a throne-hall window with a page pasted behind its glass

ra_gada_encampment.name: Ra Gada Encampment
ra_gada_encampment.site: A camp on the Yokudan desert's edge, sand-coloured tents, a drill-yard and a training-post carved with four forms.
ra_gada_encampment.mystery: Three forms are carved with students' names. The fourth, 'taught on the water,' has no name. A master's sandal sits on the step.
clues: a training-post with three names and one blank
a master's sandal on a step, dust on its strap
a drill-yard marked with a lesson's circle
ra_gada_encampment.payoff: A master's sandal: a token of the lesson.
ra_gada_encampment.rumour: At the Ra Gada camp they will tell you the fourth form is taught on the water, and then they stop speaking.
ra_gada_encampment.thread_clue: a drill-post with a ledger page nailed beneath its crossbar

hundings_dojo.name: Hunding's Dojo
hundings_dojo.site: A sunken courtyard dojo on a Yokudan island with a bowl of sand, a ring of columns, tiers of benches and a single bright pavilion.
hundings_dojo.mystery: The dojo teaches the second form. Its master has taught it a thousand times, and the last lesson, he says, was never given because no student remained long enough.
clues: a sand bowl raked into a spiral
a pavilion with a single cushion
a master who bows to an empty bench
hundings_dojo.payoff: The second form's token: a polished stone.
hundings_dojo.rumour: The sand bowl at Hunding's dojo is raked in a spiral every dawn. The master bows to an empty bench and no one has told him it is empty.

temple_of_satakal.name: Temple of Satakal
temple_of_satakal.site: A temple to the world-eater snake on an island, its roof a great coil and its floor a mosaic of scales.
temple_of_satakal.mystery: The third form is danced on the scales, and the dance ends at the snake's mouth. The priests say the student must be willing to be swallowed.
clues: a coil-roof wound about the mosaic
a mouth-shaped door at the dance's end
priests who smile and ask nothing
temple_of_satakal.payoff: The third form's token: a scale.
temple_of_satakal.rumour: The temple's priests teach a dance on a floor of scales. They say it ends where it should.
temple_of_satakal.thread_clue: a threshold tile with a tide-glyph and a navigator's mark

sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.name: Sunken Temple of the Yokudan Kings
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.site: A sunken sea-temple of flooded halls, coral shelves and air pockets, with a king's funeral barge filling the central hall and walls carved with a voyage.
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.mystery: The barge is the lesson's last classroom. Its oars are carved with the forms. The student who rows it out through the sea-gate finishes the lesson, and brings the kings home.
clues: a barge with oars carved with four forms
walls carved with a voyage's phases
an air-pocket with a master's sandal pair, one missing
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.payoff: The final form and a unique Ra Gada blade: Claw of Alkosh.
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.rumour: The sunken temple's barge has never left. The Ra Gada say it is waiting for someone who has finished their lessons.
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.thread_clue: a funeral barge with nine page-shaped hollows in its deck
